description: Lowers LDL ('bad') cholesterol and triglycerides and raises HDL to reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke.
typical_dosage: 10-80 mg by mouth once daily; dose individualized to cholesterol goal and risk category.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for cardiovascular risk reduction.
directions_for_use: Take at approximately the same time each day, with or without food.
May be taken any time of day, but pick one time and stick with it.
Swallow tablet whole; do not crush or chew.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature (68-77°F/20-25°C) in a tightly closed container, away from moisture and light.
contraindications: Active liver disease or unexplained persistent elevated liver enzymes
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness (possible myopathy/rhabdomyolysis) - especially with fever or dark urine
Signs of liver injury: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue, right upper abdominal pain
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit juice in large amounts - can raise statin levels and myopathy risk.
Alcohol in excess may add to liver-related risk.
Check with pharmacist before starting any new OTC supplement, especially red yeast rice (contains a natural statin).
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop and call the prescriber promptly for unexplained muscle pain/weakness or signs of liver injury.
Do not stop statin therapy on your own for mild effects - discuss with your pharmacist or prescriber first.
self_monitoring: Report new or worsening muscle symptoms right away.
Keep scheduled lab appointments for liver enzymes and cholesterol panels.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose - then skip the missed dose. Do not double up.

description: Lowers LDL cholesterol and triglycerides to reduce cardiovascular risk.
typical_dosage: 10-40 mg by mouth once daily in the evening (80 mg reserved for patients already tolerating it, due to myopathy risk).
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take in the evening; cholesterol synthesis is highest overnight.
May be taken with or without food.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture and light.
contraindications: Concurrent strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., certain antifungals, some antibiotics)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness (myopathy/rhabdomyolysis risk is dose- and interaction-dependent)
Signs of liver injury: jaundice, dark urine, severe fatigue
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit juice - can significantly raise simvastatin levels.
Dose is capped at 20 mg when combined with amlodipine due to increased myopathy risk.
action_if_adverse_effects: Report unexplained muscle symptoms immediately, especially if you start a new medication.
self_monitoring: Watch for new muscle pain, especially after any new prescription is added.
Attend scheduled lipid and liver panels.
missed_dose_instructions: If remembered same day, take it; if it's the next day, skip the missed dose and resume schedule. Do not double up.

description: Relaxes blood vessels to lower blood pressure and protect the heart and kidneys, especially in heart failure and diabetes.
typical_dosage: 10-40 mg by mouth once daily, titrated to blood pressure response.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time every day, with or without food.
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness, especially with the first doses.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: History of angioedema with ACE inhibitors
Concurrent use with aliskiren in diabetic patients
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Swelling of face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing/swallowing (angioedema) - seek emergency care immediately
Persistent dry cough that is bothersome
Signs of high potassium: muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid potassium supplements and salt substitutes containing potassium unless directed by prescriber - risk of hyperkalemia.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) can blunt blood-pressure-lowering effect and stress the kidneys - use acetaminophen for pain when possible.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for facial/throat swelling or breathing trouble.
Call prescriber for a persistent cough or signs of high potassium; do not stop abruptly without guidance.
self_monitoring: Check blood pressure at home if recommended and keep a log.
Report unusual swelling right away.
Keep scheduled potassium/kidney function labs.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: Lowers blood pressure and protects kidneys, often used when ACE inhibitors cause cough.
typical_dosage: 50-100 mg by mouth once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time daily, with or without food.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Concurrent use with aliskiren in diabetic patients
Do not combine with an ACE inhibitor (e.g., lisinopril)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Facial/throat swelling or trouble breathing (rare angioedema)
Signs of high potassium (muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat)
Dizziness/fainting
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid potassium supplements/salt substitutes unless directed.
NSAIDs may reduce effectiveness and stress kidneys.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for swelling/breathing trouble.
Call prescriber for persistent dizziness or fainting.
self_monitoring: Home blood pressure log if recommended.
Keep kidney function/potassium labs as scheduled.
missed_dose_instructions: Take when remembered unless near the next dose, then skip it. Do not double up.

description: Relaxes blood vessels to lower blood pressure and treat angina (chest pain).
typical_dosage: 2.5-10 mg by mouth once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Significant swelling of legs/ankles
Chest pain that worsens after starting therapy
Rapid or irregular heartbeat
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid grapefruit juice in large amounts - can raise drug levels.
Simvastatin dose should be capped at 20 mg when combined.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call prescriber for significant swelling or worsening chest pain.
Seek emergency care for fainting or a very rapid/irregular heartbeat.
self_monitoring: Home blood pressure log if recommended.
Watch for and report increasing ankle swelling.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose, then skip it. Do not double up.

description: Slows heart rate and lowers blood pressure; used for hypertension, angina, and after heart attack.
typical_dosage: 25-100 mg by mouth twice daily (immediate-release), titrated to heart rate/blood pressure.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take with or immediately after meals at consistent times.
Do not stop abruptly - must be tapered by prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Severe bradycardia or heart block without a pacemaker
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Very slow heart rate, fainting, or severe dizziness
Difficulty breathing or wheezing
Signs of worsening heart failure (swelling, shortness of breath, rapid weight gain)
otc_and_other_interactions: Can mask symptoms of low blood sugar (rapid heartbeat) in patients on insulin/sulfonylureas.
NSAIDs may reduce blood-pressure-lowering effect.
Decongestants (pseudoephedrine) may raise blood pressure/heart rate - use caution.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call prescriber for resting heart rate under 50 bpm, fainting, or worsening breathing.
Never stop abruptly - can cause rebound high blood pressure or chest pain.
self_monitoring: Check pulse/blood pressure at home if recommended before each dose.
Track weight daily if history of heart failure.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose, then skip it. Do not double up.

description: A 'water pill' that lowers blood pressure and reduces fluid retention.
typical_dosage: 12.5-25 mg by mouth once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take in the morning to avoid nighttime urination.
May be taken with food to reduce stomach upset.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of low potassium/sodium: muscle cramps, weakness, confusion, irregular heartbeat
Severe dizziness or fainting
Signs of gout flare (sudden joint pain/swelling)
otc_and_other_interactions: NSAIDs can reduce effectiveness and raise kidney risk.
Avoid excess licorice and monitor potassium if using potassium-depleting laxatives.
Increases sensitivity to sunlight - use sunscreen.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call prescriber for muscle cramping/weakness, confusion, or a fast/irregular heartbeat.
Seek care for severe dizziness or fainting.
self_monitoring: Home blood pressure log if recommended.
Keep scheduled electrolyte/kidney labs.
Weigh yourself regularly if you have heart failure.
missed_dose_instructions: Take when remembered; if late in the day, consider skipping to avoid nighttime urination and resume next morning - ask your pharmacist.

description: A potent 'water pill' used for fluid overload from heart failure, kidney, or liver disease.
typical_dosage: 20-80 mg by mouth once or twice daily, individualized to fluid status.
typical_duration: Often long-term for chronic fluid management; duration set by prescriber.
directions_for_use: Take in the morning (and early afternoon if twice daily) to avoid nighttime urination.
Take with food if it upsets your stomach.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; protect tablets from light. Do not use oral solution if discolored.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of dehydration or low potassium: severe thirst, muscle cramps, irregular heartbeat, confusion
Significant hearing changes (ringing, hearing loss) - rare, dose-related
Severe dizziness or fainting
otc_and_other_interactions: NSAIDs can blunt diuretic effect and increase kidney risk.
Increases sensitivity to sunlight.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call prescriber urgently for signs of dehydration, low potassium, or hearing changes.
Seek emergency care for fainting or a very irregular heartbeat.
self_monitoring: Weigh yourself daily at the same time; report rapid gain/loss.
Track fluid intake/output if instructed.
Keep scheduled electrolyte/kidney labs.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered; if it's late in the day, ask your pharmacist whether to skip it to avoid nighttime urination.

description: A 'blood thinner' that prevents dangerous blood clots (e.g., stroke, DVT, pulmonary embolism).
typical_dosage: Highly individualized (often 1-10 mg daily) and adjusted based on INR blood test results.
typical_duration: Varies from a few months (e.g., after a DVT) to lifelong (e.g., mechanical heart valve, atrial fibrillation).
directions_for_use: Take at the same time every day, typically in the evening.
Keep your diet consistent in vitamin K-containing foods (leafy greens) rather than avoiding them entirely - sudden changes affect INR.
Never change your dose without prescriber guidance.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protected from light and moisture.
contraindications: Recent major surgery or high fall risk without close monitoring
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Any unusual bleeding or bruising: blood in urine/stool, black tarry stools, coughing/vomiting blood, heavy nosebleeds
Severe headache, weakness, or vision changes (possible bleeding stroke)
Purple/dark skin patches (rare skin necrosis) early in therapy
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid aspirin, ibuprofen, naproxen, and other NSAIDs unless specifically directed - major bleeding risk.
Regular/high-dose acetaminophen use can raise INR - use the lowest effective dose and inform your pharmacist.
Many antibiotics (e.g., sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim, ciprofloxacin, azithromycin) can significantly raise INR - flag any new antibiotic prescription.
Avoid herbal supplements (vitamin E, fish oil, ginkgo, garlic supplements) without checking first.
Limit alcohol intake.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for serious bleeding, black stools, or neurologic symptoms.
Tell every prescriber and pharmacist you see that you take warfarin before starting any new medication, including OTC products.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled INR blood draws - missing them is dangerous.
Watch for and report any unusual bruising or bleeding.
Carry a warfarin/anticoagulant alert card.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose the same day if remembered. If not remembered until the next day, skip it - do NOT double up. Record the missed dose and tell the anticoagulation clinic/prescriber.

description: A 'blood thinner' that prevents stroke in atrial fibrillation and treats/prevents blood clots, without requiring routine blood monitoring.
typical_dosage: 5 mg twice daily (2.5 mg twice daily in certain patients based on age, weight, kidney function).
typical_duration: Often long-term/lifelong for atrial fibrillation; defined course for DVT/PE treatment.
directions_for_use: Take at the same times every day, approximately 12 hours apart, with or without food.
Do not stop without talking to your prescriber - stopping suddenly raises clot risk.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Unusual bleeding: blood in urine/stool, black tarry stools, coughing/vomiting blood
Severe headache, weakness, or confusion (possible bleeding stroke)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid aspirin, ibuprofen, naproxen, and other NSAIDs unless specifically directed - major bleeding risk.
Avoid herbal supplements that thin the blood (fish oil, vitamin E, ginkgo) without checking first.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for serious bleeding or neurologic symptoms.
Inform every provider you take this before any procedure or new medication.
self_monitoring: Watch for and report unusual bruising or bleeding.
Carry an anticoagulant alert card.
missed_dose_instructions: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered on the same day; if it's almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one and resume schedule - do not double up.

description: Prevents platelets from clumping together, reducing risk of clot-related heart attack and stroke, often after a stent.
typical_dosage: 75 mg by mouth once daily.
typical_duration: Duration set by cardiologist - often 6-12+ months after a stent; do not stop early without approval.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Unusual bleeding or bruising
Black tarry stools or blood in stool/urine
Signs of TTP (rare): fever, weakness, confusion, purple spots on skin
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid aspirin, ibuprofen, naproxen unless your cardiologist has specifically prescribed dual therapy - bleeding risk.
Omeprazole and some other PPIs may reduce clopidogrel's effectiveness - discuss alternatives (e.g., famotidine) with your pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for significant bleeding.
Never stop this medication early (especially after a stent) without cardiologist approval - risk of stent clotting.
self_monitoring: Watch for unusual bruising/bleeding.
Tell your dentist/surgeon you take this before any procedure.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered the same day; if not until the next day, skip the missed dose and continue as scheduled. Do not double up.

description: Low-dose 'baby aspirin' used to reduce risk of heart attack and stroke by preventing platelet clumping.
typical_dosage: 81 mg by mouth once daily as directed by your prescriber.
typical_duration: Ongoing, long-term preventive use.
directions_for_use: Take with food or milk if it upsets your stomach.
Enteric-coated tablets should be swallowed whole, not crushed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in a dry place; discard if tablets smell like vinegar.
contraindications: Active peptic ulcer or GI bleeding
Children/teens with viral illness (Reye syndrome risk)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Black/tarry stools, vomiting blood (GI bleeding)
Ringing in ears or hearing changes (toxicity sign)
Signs of allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with other NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) or anticoagulants (warfarin, apixaban) significantly raises bleeding risk - tell your pharmacist about all medications before combining.
Do not start or stop this without checking with your prescriber if you take other blood thinners.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop and seek care for signs of GI bleeding or ringing in the ears.
Ask your pharmacist before adding any other NSAID.
self_monitoring: Watch for dark stools or unusual bruising.
Report any new bleeding symptoms.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered; if near the next dose, skip it. Do not double up.

description: Lowers blood sugar in type 2 diabetes by reducing glucose production by the liver and improving insulin sensitivity.
typical_dosage: 500-2000 mg by mouth daily in divided doses (or once daily for extended-release), titrated to tolerance and blood sugar.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take with meals to reduce stomach upset.
Swallow extended-release tablets whole - do not crush or chew.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Before/after procedures using IV contrast dye (hold temporarily as directed)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of lactic acidosis (rare but serious): unusual muscle pain, trouble breathing, severe tiredness, stomach pain with nausea/vomiting
Signs of low blood sugar are uncommon with metformin alone but possible if combined with other diabetes drugs
otc_and_other_interactions: Limit alcohol - increases risk of lactic acidosis and low blood sugar.
Tell your radiology department and pharmacist if you are having a CT scan or procedure with IV contrast dye - metformin may need to be held.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of lactic acidosis.
Call prescriber if GI side effects don't improve after a few weeks.
self_monitoring: Check blood sugar as directed and keep a log.
Keep scheduled kidney function and vitamin B12 labs (long-term use can lower B12).
missed_dose_instructions: Take with your next meal if remembered same day; if it's almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one. Do not double up.

description: Stimulates the pancreas to release more insulin, lowering blood sugar in type 2 diabetes.
typical_dosage: 2.5-20 mg by mouth once or twice daily, taken 30 minutes before a meal.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take about 30 minutes before breakfast (or the first main meal).
Do not skip meals after taking a dose - raises low blood sugar risk.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture and light.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of low blood sugar: shakiness, sweating, confusion, rapid heartbeat, fainting
Severe skin reaction or jaundice (rare)
otc_and_other_interactions: Alcohol can cause severe low blood sugar and flushing reactions - avoid or use with caution.
Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim and certain fluoroquinolone antibiotics (e.g., ciprofloxacin) can significantly increase the risk of low blood sugar.
action_if_adverse_effects: Treat low blood sugar immediately with fast-acting sugar (juice, glucose tablets); seek emergency care if confusion or loss of consciousness occurs.
Call prescriber if low blood sugar episodes are frequent.
self_monitoring: Check blood sugar as directed, especially before meals and driving.
Carry a fast-acting sugar source at all times.
Wear medical alert identification.
missed_dose_instructions: If a meal was skipped, skip that dose too. Otherwise take as soon as remembered; if close to the next meal/dose, skip it. Do not double up.

description: A long-acting insulin that provides steady, background blood sugar control over about 24 hours.
typical_dosage: Individualized starting dose (often 10 units or weight-based) once daily, titrated by prescriber based on blood glucose.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Inject at the same time every day into the abdomen, thigh, or upper arm, rotating sites.
Do not mix with other insulins in the same syringe.
Use a new needle for each injection and dispose of used needles in a sharps container.
storage_instructions: Refrigerate unopened pens/vials (36-46°F/2-8°C); do not freeze. Once in use, may be kept at room temperature (up to 86°F/30°C) and discarded after the labeled in-use period (commonly 28 days) - check your specific product's labeling.
contraindications: Episodes of hypoglycemia currently in progress
Known hypersensitivity to this insulin product
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of low blood sugar: shakiness, sweating, confusion, rapid heartbeat, seizure, loss of consciousness
Signs of severe allergic reaction at injection site or systemically
otc_and_other_interactions: Alcohol can increase the risk and severity of low blood sugar.
Beta-blockers (e.g., metoprolol) can mask the warning signs of low blood sugar.
action_if_adverse_effects: Treat low blood sugar immediately with fast-acting sugar; seek emergency help for seizure or unconsciousness.
Report severe injection site reactions to your prescriber.
self_monitoring: Check blood glucose as directed and keep a log.
Rotate injection sites to avoid skin changes.
Carry a fast-acting sugar source and wear medical alert ID.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, contact your prescriber or diabetes care team for guidance rather than guessing - do not double the next dose.

description: Replaces thyroid hormone in patients with an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism).
typical_dosage: Individualized dose (often 25-200 mcg) once daily based on lab monitoring (TSH).
typical_duration: Usually lifelong replacement therapy.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, 30-60 minutes before breakfast, with a full glass of water.
Take consistently at the same time each day and stay on the same brand/formulation when possible.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Chest pain, rapid/irregular heartbeat
Signs of too much thyroid hormone: tremor, heat intolerance, significant weight loss, anxiety
Signs of too little effect: fatigue, weight gain, constipation, cold intolerance
common_side_effects: Usually well tolerated at correct dose; symptoms typically indicate dose is too high or low
otc_and_other_interactions: Calcium and iron supplements/antacids reduce absorption - separate by at least 4 hours.
Omeprazole and other acid reducers can reduce absorption - take levothyroxine consistently relative to these.
Do not switch brands without telling your pharmacist - bioavailability can differ.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call prescriber for symptoms of over- or under-treatment rather than adjusting the dose yourself.
Seek care for chest pain or a rapid irregular heartbeat.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled TSH lab draws (typically 6-8 weeks after any dose change).
Track symptoms of over/under-treatment.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered that day; if not remembered until the next day, take one dose only (do not double up) and resume schedule.

description: Reduces stomach acid production to treat heartburn, GERD, and ulcers.
typical_dosage: 20-40 mg by mouth once daily, before a meal.
typical_duration: OTC use limited to 14-day courses (up to 3x/year) unless directed otherwise by a prescriber; Rx use may be longer-term.
directions_for_use: Take 30-60 minutes before a meal, usually breakfast.
Swallow capsule whole - do not crush or chew (delayed-release coating).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Concurrent use with rilpivirine (an HIV medication)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe or persistent diarrhea (possible C. difficile infection)
New or worsening bone pain/fracture with long-term use
Signs of low magnesium: muscle spasms, irregular heartbeat, seizures - with long-term use
otc_and_other_interactions: Reduces absorption of levothyroxine, iron, and vitamin B12 - separate dosing as advised.
May reduce the effectiveness of clopidogrel - discuss alternatives with your pharmacist if you take both.
Do not use for more than 14 days without medical advice unless prescribed long-term.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call prescriber for severe diarrhea or symptoms lasting beyond the OTC treatment course.
Report bone pain or muscle spasms with long-term use.
self_monitoring: Track symptom improvement; if no relief within 14 days of OTC use, see a prescriber.
With long-term use, periodic magnesium/B12 monitoring may be recommended.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered; if near the next dose, skip the missed one. Do not double up.

description: Reduces stomach acid to relieve and prevent heartburn and treat ulcers/GERD.
typical_dosage: 10-20 mg by mouth once or twice daily; up to 40 mg twice daily for prescription indications.
typical_duration: OTC use typically short-term (up to 2 weeks) unless directed otherwise.
directions_for_use: Take 15-60 minutes before meals that may cause heartburn, or at bedtime for nighttime symptoms.
Can be taken with or without food.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Difficulty swallowing, unexplained weight loss, or vomiting blood (may indicate a more serious condition)
Confusion, especially in older adults or with kidney impairment
otc_and_other_interactions: Generally fewer interactions than PPIs; still separate from drugs requiring stomach acid for absorption if advised.
action_if_adverse_effects: See a prescriber if symptoms persist beyond 2 weeks or if warning symptoms (difficulty swallowing, weight loss) occur.
self_monitoring: Track symptom frequency/severity.
Reduce dose adjustments in kidney disease should be directed by a prescriber.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered, or simply take the next dose at its scheduled time if it is being used on an as-needed basis.

description: Prevents and treats nausea and vomiting, including from chemotherapy, surgery, or illness.
typical_dosage: 4-8 mg by mouth every 8 hours as needed, or as directed around chemotherapy/surgery.
typical_duration: Short-term/as-needed use unless part of a chemotherapy regimen.
directions_for_use: For orally disintegrating tablets, let dissolve on the tongue - do not chew or swallow whole with liquid required.
Take with or without food.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fast, pounding, or irregular heartbeat, or fainting (rare QT prolongation risk)
Signs of serotonin syndrome if combined with other serotonergic drugs: agitation, rapid heartbeat, muscle twitching
otc_and_other_interactions: Can raise risk of serotonin syndrome when combined with SSRIs (e.g., sertraline) or tramadol.
Use caution with other QT-prolonging medications.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for fainting, an irregular heartbeat, or symptoms of serotonin syndrome.
self_monitoring: Track nausea/vomiting frequency and hydration status.
Report any heart palpitations.
missed_dose_instructions: This is usually taken as needed; if on a scheduled regimen and a dose is missed, take it when remembered unless close to the next dose.

description: Softens stool to relieve and prevent constipation by allowing water and fat to mix into the stool.
typical_dosage: 50-300 mg by mouth daily in divided doses.
typical_duration: Short-term use for occasional constipation; can be used longer-term as directed for chronic conditions.
directions_for_use: Take with a full glass of water.
Drink adequate fluids throughout the day for best effect.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Undiagnosed abdominal pain, nausea, or vomiting
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe abdominal pain or cramping
Rectal bleeding or no improvement after several days
common_side_effects: Throat irritation with liquid form if not diluted
otc_and_other_interactions: Generally minimal drug interactions; avoid taking at the same time as mineral oil.
action_if_adverse_effects: See a prescriber if constipation persists beyond 1 week or is accompanied by severe pain/bleeding.
self_monitoring: Track bowel movement frequency.
Ensure adequate fluid and fiber intake.
missed_dose_instructions: Not typically critical if used for occasional constipation; resume normal use as needed.

description: A rescue inhaler that quickly relaxes airway muscles to relieve wheezing and shortness of breath in asthma/COPD.
typical_dosage: 1-2 inhalations every 4-6 hours as needed for symptoms; 2 inhalations 15-30 minutes before exercise if used preventively.
typical_duration: As-needed, ongoing rescue use.
directions_for_use: Shake well before each use.
Prime the inhaler before first use and if not used for more than 14 days.
Use a spacer if recommended, especially for children.
Rinse mouth after use if also using an inhaled steroid.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; avoid extreme heat (do not leave in a hot car) - canister may burst.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Chest pain or a fast/irregular heartbeat
Wheezing/shortness of breath that worsens or does not improve after use (may signal a serious asthma attack - seek emergency care)
Using more than the prescribed amount to control symptoms (sign of worsening disease - contact prescriber)
otc_and_other_interactions: Other stimulants (e.g., decongestants like pseudoephedrine) can add to jitteriness/heart racing.
Beta-blockers (e.g., metoprolol) can reduce albuterol's effectiveness.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care if breathing does not improve after use or symptoms rapidly worsen.
Contact prescriber if you are using your rescue inhaler more than twice a week - asthma control may need adjustment.
self_monitoring: Track how often you need to use the rescue inhaler.
Know the number of actuations remaining (track doses used) since canisters do not always show a reliable fill level.
missed_dose_instructions: This is used as needed for symptoms, not on a fixed schedule - use when symptoms occur, following prescribed maximum frequency.

description: Reduces nasal inflammation to relieve allergy symptoms: sneezing, congestion, runny/itchy nose.
typical_dosage: 1-2 sprays per nostril once daily.
typical_duration: May take several days for full effect; can be used seasonally or longer-term for chronic allergies.
directions_for_use: Shake gently, blow nose first, tilt head slightly forward, spray into each nostril while sniffing gently, aim away from the nasal septum.
Use at the same time each day for best effect - benefits build over days.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, do not freeze; shake before use.
contraindications: Recent nasal surgery or injury (until healed)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Recurrent nosebleeds or nasal sores
Vision changes (rare, with long-term use - glaucoma/cataract risk)
Whistling sound from a hole in the nasal septum (rare)
otc_and_other_interactions: Minimal systemic drug interactions at recommended doses; avoid combining multiple nasal steroid products.

typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy with regular monitoring.

Fainting, very slow heart rate, or worsening irregular heartbeat

missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, contact the prescriber's office for guidance rather than guessing, given the narrow dosing margin of this medication; do not double up on your own.

description: Lowers blood sugar in type 2 diabetes by causing the kidneys to remove more sugar through urine; also used to reduce kidney-related risk in some patients with chronic kidney disease.
typical_dosage: 100-300 mg by mouth once daily before the first meal of the day.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take once daily before the first meal of the day.
Maintain good genital hygiene to reduce risk of yeast infections.
Stay well hydrated, especially in hot weather or with illness.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: History of lower-limb amputation (use with caution per prescriber)

Keep scheduled kidney function labs.

description: Helps control blood sugar in type 2 diabetes and/or supports weight management by slowing digestion and increasing feelings of fullness.

typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.

self_monitoring: Check blood sugar as directed.
Track weight and appetite changes.
Watch for persistent GI symptoms or dehydration.

description: A form of insulin used to help control blood sugar in diabetes; this rapid-acting form starts working quickly and is usually given shortly before meals.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and titrated by the prescriber based on blood sugar patterns, meals, and activity; do not adjust the dose or schedule without guidance.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed.
directions_for_use: Inject subcutaneously into the abdomen, thigh, upper arm, or buttock, rotating injection sites to avoid skin changes.

Check the appearance of the insulin before each use per manufacturer instructions; do not use if discolored or containing particles unless the product is normally cloudy (e.g., NPH) and has been properly resuspended.
Never share insulin pens or needles, even between vials, due to infection risk.
Carry a fast-acting source of sugar at all times in case of low blood sugar.
storage_instructions: Store unopened insulin in the refrigerator; do not freeze. In-use (opened) insulin may be kept at room temperature for a limited time per manufacturer labeling, away from direct heat and light.
contraindications: Episodes of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) without correction first
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe low blood sugar: confusion, seizure, loss of consciousness - seek emergency care
Signs of severe allergic reaction: whole-body rash, facial/throat swelling, difficulty breathing
Significant swelling or rapid weight gain
otc_and_other_interactions: Alcohol can increase the risk and severity of low blood sugar.
Certain OTC cold/decongestant products may raise blood sugar slightly; check with a pharmacist.
NSAIDs and aspirin in high doses may slightly enhance insulin's blood-sugar-lowering effect.
action_if_adverse_effects: Treat low blood sugar immediately with fast-acting sugar; seek emergency care if severe or not improving.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Check blood sugar as directed, especially before doses and at bedtime.
Learn the signs of low and high blood sugar and how to respond.
Rotate injection sites and inspect skin for lumps or changes.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact the prescriber or diabetes care team for guidance on a missed insulin dose rather than guessing, since timing depends on the specific insulin and meal schedule.

description: Slows the breakdown and absorption of carbohydrates in the gut, helping to reduce the rise in blood sugar after meals in type 2 diabetes.
typical_dosage: 25-100 mg by mouth 3 times daily, taken with the first bite of each main meal, titrated by prescriber.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take with the first bite of each main meal, not before or after.
If low blood sugar occurs while on this medication in combination with other diabetes drugs, treat with glucose (not table sugar), since acarbose blocks the breakdown of regular sugar.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Bowel obstruction or predisposition to obstruction
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Yellowing of skin/eyes (rare liver problems)
Severe abdominal pain or bloating
Signs of low blood sugar if used with other diabetes medications: confusion, sweating, shakiness
otc_and_other_interactions: If low blood sugar occurs while taking this medication with a sulfonylurea or insulin, use glucose tablets/gel rather than table sugar or juice, which will not be absorbed quickly enough.
Digestive enzyme or charcoal-containing OTC products may reduce this medication's effect.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call prescriber for persistent GI symptoms or signs of liver problems.
Treat low blood sugar with glucose tablets/gel; seek care if not improving.
self_monitoring: Check blood sugar as directed, particularly after meals.
Keep scheduled liver function labs.
Track GI symptoms, which often improve over time.
missed_dose_instructions: If a meal is missed, skip the dose for that meal; do not take extra at the next meal to make up for it.

description: Replaces or supplements thyroid hormone in people with low thyroid function (hypothyroidism); faster-acting than levothyroxine.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and titrated by the prescriber based on thyroid lab results and symptoms; do not adjust the dose or schedule without guidance.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for most patients.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, at the same time each day, typically in the morning.

description: Slows bone breakdown to help prevent and treat osteoporosis and reduce the risk of fractures.
typical_dosage: 70 mg by mouth once weekly, or 10 mg once daily, as directed.
typical_duration: Long-term therapy; prescriber may periodically reassess ongoing need after several years.
directions_for_use: Take first thing in the morning on an empty stomach with a full glass (6-8 oz) of plain water only.
Remain upright (sitting or standing) for at least 30-60 minutes after taking, and do not lie down.
Do not eat, drink anything other than plain water, or take other medications/supplements for at least 30-60 minutes after the dose, as directed by prescriber/pharmacist.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Inability to sit or stand upright for at least 30-60 minutes
Esophageal abnormalities that delay emptying (e.g., stricture, achalasia)
Low blood calcium (must be corrected before starting)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Chest pain, new or worsening heartburn, or difficulty/pain with swallowing (esophageal irritation)
Severe or unusual thigh, hip, or groin pain (rare atypical fracture)
Jaw pain, swelling, or numbness, especially after dental work (rare osteonecrosis of the jaw)
otc_and_other_interactions: Calcium supplements, antacids, and multivitamins containing calcium, iron, or magnesium reduce absorption - separate by at least 30-60 minutes.
NSAIDs may increase stomach irritation when combined with this medication.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop and call prescriber for chest pain, swallowing difficulty, or severe bone pain.
Tell your dentist you take this medication before any dental procedures.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled bone density scans and calcium/vitamin D level checks.
Report new hip, thigh, or jaw pain.
Maintain adequate calcium and vitamin D intake as advised.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose on the regular scheduled day; do not take two doses on the same day or take it later that day.

Avoid skin-to-skin contact with others (especially women and children) at the application site until the gel has dried; wash any exposed skin promptly if contact occurs.

Pregnancy or breastfeeding (should not be used by or transferred to women/children)

Difficulty urinating or other signs of prostate enlargement

Watch for skin reactions at the application site.
Prevent contact between the application site and others until dry.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply as soon as remembered that day; if not remembered until the next day, skip the missed dose and resume the normal daily schedule - do not apply a double amount.

directions_for_use: Take with or without food.
Complete the full course as prescribed.
Avoid tyramine-rich foods (aged cheese, cured meats, tap beer) during treatment.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light.

Concurrent use of serotonergic drugs without medical guidance
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of serotonin syndrome: agitation, rapid heartbeat, fever, muscle rigidity (especially with antidepressants)
Signs of low blood counts: unusual bruising, bleeding, infection, fatigue (with prolonged use)
Numbness, tingling, or vision changes with long-term use
Signs of lactic acidosis: rapid breathing, nausea, severe fatigue

action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of serotonin syndrome.
Call prescriber for unusual bleeding/bruising or numbness.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled blood count checks, especially if the course exceeds 2 weeks.
Watch for vision changes with long-term use.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

description: An antifungal medication used to treat yeast and fungal infections, including vaginal yeast infections, oral/esophageal thrush, and systemic fungal infections.

typical_duration: Single dose for uncomplicated vaginal yeast infection; days to weeks for other infections.
directions_for_use: Take with or without food.
Complete the full prescribed course for multi-day regimens.

Irregular heartbeat (QT prolongation)

action_if_adverse_effects: Call prescriber for signs of liver problems or irregular heartbeat.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Watch for yellowing of skin/eyes or unusual fatigue.
missed_dose_instructions: For a single-dose regimen, no missed dose applies. For multi-day regimens, take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up.

description: An antifungal medication used to treat fungal infections of the nails, skin, and other body systems.

storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.

severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of heart failure: swelling of legs/feet, shortness of breath, unusual fatigue

Hearing changes (rare)

action_if_adverse_effects: Call prescriber for signs of heart failure or liver problems.
self_monitoring: Watch for swelling, shortness of breath, or yellowing of skin/eyes.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

description: An antifungal medication used to treat oral thrush and other localized Candida (yeast) infections; it is not absorbed into the bloodstream.

Use after meals and at bedtime for best contact with affected areas.
Keep an even dosing schedule.

severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of an allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing (rare)
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected since nystatin is minimally absorbed; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.

missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

description: An antifungal medication used to treat fungal infections of the skin (athlete's foot, ringworm, jock itch) with topical forms, and nail fungus with oral tablets.

Severe skin reaction
Persistent taste or smell changes (rare, oral use)

Discontinue topical use and consult a pharmacist for severe irritation.
self_monitoring: For oral use, keep scheduled liver function tests if recommended.
Track nail or skin improvement.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

Avoid alcohol - can cause flushing or rapid heartbeat.
Use sunscreen due to increased sun sensitivity.

self_monitoring: Track fungal infection improvement.
Report persistent headache or rash.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

description: An antiviral medication used to treat and suppress herpes virus infections, including cold sores, genital herpes, and shingles.

Drink plenty of fluids.
Take at evenly spaced intervals.

severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of kidney problems: decreased urination, swelling

Maintain adequate hydration, especially when also taking NSAIDs, to reduce kidney stress.

self_monitoring: Track outbreak healing.
Stay well hydrated.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

Drink plenty of fluids.
Take at evenly spaced intervals.

Stay well hydrated.

description: An antiviral medication used to treat herpes virus infections, including cold sores, genital herpes, and shingles.

Stay well hydrated.

description: An antiviral medication used to treat and help prevent influenza (flu); works best when started within 48 hours of symptom onset.

Start as soon as possible after symptom onset.
Complete the full course.

Signs of a severe allergic reaction

Stop and seek emergency care for signs of an allergic reaction.

Track fever and symptom improvement.

description: A combination antiviral medication used to treat mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in people at higher risk for severe disease; must be started within 5 days of symptom onset.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and follows the prescriber's exact packaged regimen (commonly nirmatrelvir 300 mg plus ritonavir 100 mg by mouth twice daily), adjusted for kidney function; do not adjust the dose or schedule without guidance.
typical_duration: 5 days.
directions_for_use: Take both tablets together exactly as packaged, twice daily.
Complete the full 5-day course.
Ritonavir strongly affects how the liver processes many other drugs - review all medications and supplements with a pharmacist before starting.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Severe liver or kidney impairment (per prescriber)
Use with many drugs that depend heavily on the same liver enzyme (e.g., certain statins, some heart rhythm medications) - significant interaction risk
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of a severe allergic reaction
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue

action_if_adverse_effects: Call prescriber for any new or unusual symptoms after starting.
Seek emergency care for signs of a severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track COVID-19 symptoms.
Report rebound symptoms to the prescriber if concerning.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact prescriber for guidance rather than guessing, since this is a short, fixed 5-day course and timing matters for effectiveness.

description: An antiviral medication used to treat mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in adults at higher risk for severe disease; must be started within 5 days of symptom onset.

Not recommended during pregnancy.

severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of a severe allergic reaction
Severe or persistent diarrhea/nausea

self_monitoring: Track COVID-19 symptoms and completion of the full 5-day course.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact prescriber for guidance rather than guessing, since this is a short, fixed 5-day course.

description: A combination antiviral medication used to treat chronic hepatitis C virus infection.
typical_dosage: One tablet by mouth once daily, per the prescriber's exact regimen and duration.
typical_duration: Usually 12 weeks; do not stop early even if feeling well - the full course is needed to cure the infection and prevent resistance.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Do not stop without consulting the prescriber.
Avoid acid-reducing medications unless approved by the prescriber, since they can lower drug levels.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Concurrent use with certain drugs that reduce absorption (e.g., some acid reducers, certain seizure or tuberculosis medications)
Concurrent use with amiodarone (risk of dangerously slow heart rate)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of worsening liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, severe fatigue
Very slow heart rate, dizziness, or fainting if combined with amiodarone
Signs of hepatitis B reactivation in co-infected patients
otc_and_other_interactions: Antacids, H2 blockers (e.g., famotidine), and proton pump inhibitors (e.g., omeprazole) can reduce absorption and effectiveness - take antacids at least 4 hours apart and discuss H2 blocker/PPI timing with a pharmacist.
St. John's Wort can significantly reduce effectiveness - avoid.

Seek emergency care for severe dizziness or fainting.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled hepatitis C viral load labs.
Track completion of the full course.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered on the same day; if not remembered until the next day, skip the missed dose and continue the regular schedule - do not double up. Contact prescriber if multiple doses are missed.

severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of kidney problems: decreased urination, swelling

Signs of liver problems, including worsening hepatitis B if stopped abruptly in co-infected patients

Seek emergency care for signs of lactic acidosis.

Take doses consistently to maintain effectiveness.

description: A complete single-tablet combination medication used to treat HIV infection.

Take doses consistently to maintain effectiveness.

description: A topical treatment for head lice (OTC) and scabies (prescription).

Eye irritation if accidental contact occurs

description: Relieves pain and inflammation, commonly used for osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis.

Monitor blood pressure if on long-term therapy.

description: Relieves pain and inflammation from arthritis and other conditions, with somewhat lower GI bleeding risk than nonselective NSAIDs.

action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for chest pain, fainting, or signs of a severe allergic reaction.
Contact the prescriber promptly for suicidal thoughts or signs of liver problems.
self_monitoring: Track mood and behavior changes, especially in children and adolescents.
Watch for signs of liver problems or unusual fatigue.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and titrated by the prescriber based on response and tolerability; do not adjust the dose or schedule without guidance.
typical_duration: Long-term for ADHD management, with periodic reassessment.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food, but consistently either with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole - do not crush, chew, or split.
Do not stop abruptly - can cause rebound high blood pressure.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fainting or very slow heartbeat
Signs of rebound high blood pressure after missed doses or stopping: headache, anxiety, rapid heartbeat
Severe drowsiness affecting daily activities
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid alcohol and sedating OTC products (e.g., diphenhydramine) - additive drowsiness and blood-pressure-lowering effect.
OTC decongestants (e.g., pseudoephedrine) may counteract the blood-pressure-lowering effect - use with caution.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for fainting or a very slow heartbeat.
Contact the prescriber for signs of rebound high blood pressure or severe drowsiness.
Do not stop abruptly - taper under prescriber supervision.
self_monitoring: Monitor blood pressure and heart rate periodically as advised.
Avoid missing doses, and never stop abruptly without guidance.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, do not double up; contact the prescriber if more than one dose in a row is missed, since restarting may need to be done gradually to avoid rebound high blood pressure.

self_monitoring: Track pain control and bowel movements; treat constipation proactively.

Keep this medication secure and never share it with others.
missed_dose_instructions: If on a scheduled regimen, take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule - do not double up. Contact the prescriber if pain becomes poorly controlled.

description: Combines an opioid with acetaminophen to treat moderate-to-severe short-term pain.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized by the prescriber based on pain severity and response; do not exceed the maximum total daily acetaminophen dose from all sources (typically 3000-4000 mg/day) and do not adjust without guidance.

Do not take any additional acetaminophen-containing products (including OTC Tylenol or combination cold/flu products) without checking total daily acetaminophen intake with a pharmacist.
Keep in a secure location; dispose of unused medication through a take-back program.

contraindications: Use with, or within 14 days of, an MAOI
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Slow, shallow, or stopped breathing, extreme drowsiness, or unresponsiveness - seek emergency care immediately; this can be fatal

Severe constipation or abdominal pain
otc_and_other_interactions: Do not take with additional OTC acetaminophen products (Tylenol, many cold/flu/sleep combinations) - risk of exceeding the maximum safe daily dose and causing liver damage.

description: A long-acting patch used to treat persistent, severe chronic pain in patients who are already tolerant to opioid therapy, by releasing medication continuously through the skin.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and titrated by the prescriber based on prior opioid tolerance and response; do not adjust the dose, patch strength, or wear schedule without guidance.
typical_duration: Used for long-term management of chronic, persistent severe pain in opioid-tolerant patients only.
directions_for_use: Apply to clean, dry, intact skin on the upper body or arm; rotate application sites.
Wear for the exact number of hours prescribed (usually 72 hours) before replacing.
Do not cut the patch, and avoid exposing the patch area to heat sources (heating pads, hot tubs, saunas) - heat increases drug release and overdose risk.
Fold used patches in half (sticky sides together) and dispose of promptly and safely - used patches still contain active medication.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture and heat; keep locked/secure and out of reach of children, pets, and others - even used patches can be fatal to a child or pet.
contraindications: Use with, or within 14 days of, an MAOI
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Slow, shallow, or stopped breathing, extreme drowsiness, or unresponsiveness - seek emergency care immediately; this can be fatal, especially with heat exposure or in opioid-naive patients
Severe confusion, hallucinations, or fainting
Signs of a fever raising drug absorption (fentanyl release increases with body temperature)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid alcohol and sedating OTC products (e.g., diphenhydramine-containing sleep aids) - additive sedation and dangerously slowed breathing.
Avoid heating pads, electric blankets, hot tubs, or saunas over or near the patch - heat significantly increases drug absorption and overdose risk.
Start a stimulant laxative or stool softener proactively for constipation.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for slow/shallow breathing or unresponsiveness; keep naloxone available if prescribed.
Remove the patch and contact the prescriber for severe confusion, fainting, or fever.
Do not stop abruptly after regular use - taper under prescriber supervision.
self_monitoring: Check the patch regularly to ensure it remains attached.
Track pain control and bowel movements.
Avoid heat sources near the patch, and monitor for fever.
missed_dose_instructions: If a patch falls off early or is due for a change, contact the prescriber's office or pharmacist for guidance rather than guessing - do not apply an extra patch on your own.

drug_class: Opioid analgesic / opioid use disorder treatment
description: A long-acting opioid used to treat chronic pain or, more commonly, to treat opioid use disorder by reducing withdrawal symptoms and cravings.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and carefully titrated by the prescriber or opioid treatment program based on response; do not adjust the dose or schedule without guidance, as effects build up gradually over days.
typical_duration: May be used short-term for pain or long-term (often indefinitely) for opioid use disorder treatment.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as prescribed or as dispensed by the opioid treatment program, at the same time each day.
Do not increase the dose on your own even if pain relief or craving control seems incomplete - the full effect of a dose change takes several days to appear.
Keep in a secure location; dispose of unused medication through a take-back program.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture; keep locked/secure and out of reach of children, pets, and others - a small amount can be fatal to a child.
contraindications: Use with, or within 14 days of, an MAOI
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Slow, shallow, or stopped breathing, extreme drowsiness, or unresponsiveness - seek emergency care immediately; risk is highest in the first two weeks of treatment or after any dose increase
Fainting, severe dizziness, or a rapid/irregular heartbeat (possible dangerous heart rhythm/QT prolongation)
Severe constipation or abdominal pain
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid alcohol and sedating OTC products (e.g., diphenhydramine-containing sleep aids) - additive sedation and dangerously slowed breathing.
Start a stimulant laxative or stool softener proactively for constipation.
Tell the pharmacist about all other medications, since methadone levels and heart rhythm effects can be significantly affected by other drugs.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for slow/shallow breathing, unresponsiveness, fainting, or an irregular heartbeat; keep naloxone available if prescribed.
Contact the prescriber or treatment program for severe constipation or persistent nausea.
Do not stop abruptly - discuss any concerns with the prescriber or program.
self_monitoring: Track pain control or craving/withdrawal control and bowel movements.
Watch for excessive drowsiness, slowed breathing, or palpitations, especially early in treatment or after a dose change.
Keep this medication secure and never share it with others.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact the prescriber or opioid treatment program if a dose is missed rather than guessing - do not double up, as methadone accumulates in the body and overdose risk increases with extra doses.

drug_class: Opioid use disorder treatment (partial opioid agonist combination)
description: Used to treat opioid use disorder by reducing withdrawal symptoms and cravings while lowering the risk of misuse; the naloxone component discourages injection misuse.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and titrated by the prescriber based on response; do not adjust the dose or schedule without guidance.
typical_duration: Often used long-term, sometimes indefinitely, as part of ongoing opioid use disorder treatment.
directions_for_use: Place under the tongue (or in the cheek, depending on product) and allow it to dissolve completely - do not chew or swallow whole.
Do not eat, drink, or smoke until the film/tablet has fully dissolved.
Must generally be in mild-to-moderate withdrawal before the first dose to avoid precipitating withdrawal - follow prescriber instructions on timing.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture; keep locked/secure and out of reach of children and others - even small amounts can be dangerous to a child.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to buprenorphine or naloxone
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Slow, shallow, or stopped breathing, extreme drowsiness, or unresponsiveness - seek emergency care immediately, especially if combined with benzodiazepines, alcohol, or other sedatives
Signs of liver problems: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, abdominal pain
Signs of a severe allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid alcohol and sedating OTC products (e.g., diphenhydramine-containing sleep aids) - additive sedation and dangerously slowed breathing.
Do not use other opioid-containing products (including some OTC cough suppressants with codeine where available) without checking with the prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for slow/shallow breathing or unresponsiveness; keep naloxone available if prescribed.
Contact the prescriber for signs of liver problems.
Do not stop abruptly without discussing with the prescriber or treatment program.
self_monitoring: Track cravings and withdrawal control, and report if symptoms return.
Watch for excessive sedation, especially if any other sedating medication is used.
missed_dose_instructions: Contact the prescriber or treatment program if a dose is missed rather than guessing about how to adjust the next dose.

description: Used in an emergency to rapidly reverse the effects of an opioid overdose, including dangerously slowed or stopped breathing.
typical_dosage: One spray (4 mg) into one nostril; may repeat with a new device every 2-3 minutes if the person does not respond or breathing does not improve, while awaiting emergency help.
typical_duration: Used only in an emergency situation for suspected opioid overdose - not for routine or scheduled use.
directions_for_use: Lay the person on their back and support their neck; tilt the head back slightly.
Insert the nozzle into one nostril and press the plunger firmly to release the full dose.
Call 911 immediately, even if the person seems to recover - opioid effects can return after naloxone wears off, and repeat doses or monitoring may be needed.
Stay with the person and be prepared to give another dose or start rescue breathing/CPR if needed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; avoid extreme heat or freezing temperatures; check the expiration date periodically and replace as needed.
contraindications: None that prevent emergency use - benefits of use in a suspected overdose outweigh risks
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of opioid withdrawal in a dependent person: rapid heartbeat, sweating, agitation, nausea, vomiting - these are expected and generally not dangerous, but the person should still be monitored
Breathing that does not improve, or that worsens again after initial improvement - call 911 and give additional doses if available
common_side_effects: Symptoms of opioid withdrawal if the person is opioid-dependent
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC drug interactions expected; naloxone works by blocking opioid effects and can precipitate withdrawal symptoms in someone who is opioid-dependent - this is an expected part of its lifesaving action, not a reason to avoid using it.
action_if_adverse_effects: Always call 911 after administering naloxone, even if the person appears to recover.
Monitor the person closely, as the opioid may outlast the naloxone and breathing problems can return.
self_monitoring: Keep naloxone accessible and know how to use it if you or someone you know is at risk of opioid overdose.
Check the expiration date periodically.
Make sure family members or household contacts know where it is kept and how to use it.
missed_dose_instructions: This medication is used only in an emergency and has no scheduled dosing - there is no 'missed dose' to worry about.

description: Used to help prevent relapse in opioid or alcohol use disorder by blocking opioid receptors, reducing cravings and the rewarding effects of opioids and alcohol.
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized by the prescriber; the patient must typically be opioid-free for 7-10 days before starting to avoid precipitating withdrawal - do not start or adjust without prescriber guidance.
typical_duration: Often used long-term as part of ongoing relapse-prevention treatment.
directions_for_use: Do not take if you have used any opioids recently - confirm required opioid-free period with the prescriber before starting or restarting.
Take the oral tablet with or without food, at the same time each day.
The extended-release injection is given by a healthcare professional once a month.
storage_instructions: Store the oral tablet at room temperature, away from moisture. The injectable suspension requires refrigeration and is prepared/administered by a healthcare provider.
contraindications: Current use of opioids or in acute opioid withdrawal
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of liver damage: yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue, abdominal pain - seek care promptly
Severe injection-site reactions (for the injectable form): significant pain, swelling, or skin breakdown
Sudden inability to achieve pain control with opioids in a true emergency - inform all emergency responders that you take this medication
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid any opioid-containing products, including some OTC cough/cold products in certain states, without prescriber guidance - this medication blocks opioid effects and can precipitate withdrawal or make opioid pain relief ineffective.
Check with a pharmacist before using any new OTC product if you have any liver concerns.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care promptly for signs of liver damage.
Carry medical identification noting naltrexone use in case of emergency, since opioid pain medications will not work as expected.
Contact the prescriber for severe injection-site reactions.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled liver function monitoring appointments.
Wear or carry medical identification indicating you take this medication.
Never attempt to overcome the opioid-blocking effect by taking large amounts of opioids - this can cause a fatal overdose.
missed_dose_instructions: For the oral tablet, take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule. For the monthly injection, contact the prescriber's office to reschedule as soon as possible.

drug_class: Opioid antagonist / aminoketone antidepressant combination (weight management)
description: Combines naltrexone and bupropion to help reduce appetite and food cravings for chronic weight management alongside diet and exercise.
dosage_forms: Extended-release tablet (8 mg naltrexone/90 mg bupropion)
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and titrated by the prescriber over about 4 weeks based on response and tolerability; do not adjust the dose or schedule without guidance.
typical_duration: Long-term use for chronic weight management; reassessed if insufficient weight loss after about 12 weeks at the full dose.
directions_for_use: Take tablets whole; do not cut, crush, or chew.
Avoid high-fat meals when taking, as this can increase drug levels.
Take in the morning and evening as directed to reduce the chance of insomnia.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Seizure disorder or conditions that lower seizure threshold
Current use of other bupropion-containing products
Chronic opioid or opiate agonist use, or acute opiate withdrawal
Bulimia or anorexia nervosa (current or history)
Use within 14 days of an MAOI
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Seizures
New or worsening suicidal thoughts, mood, or behavior changes
Signs of liver injury: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe stomach pain
Severely elevated blood pressure or heart rate
Eye pain or vision changes (possible acute glaucoma)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid alcohol - can increase seizure risk and interact with bupropion.
Do not use with other OTC weight-loss or stimulant products.
Avoid opioid-containing OTC/Rx cough or pain products - naltrexone blocks opioid effects and can precipitate withdrawal or block needed pain relief.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for a seizure, chest pain, or signs of liver injury.
Call prescriber for mood changes or new suicidal thoughts.
self_monitoring: Monitor blood pressure and heart rate periodically.
Track mood changes.
Track weight-loss progress with prescriber.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and resume the regular schedule at the next scheduled time; do not double up, and avoid taking a late-day dose to reduce insomnia.

description: Supports treatment of chronic alcohol use disorder by causing an unpleasant reaction (flushing, nausea, vomiting) if alcohol is consumed, discouraging drinking.
typical_dosage: Usually 125-500 mg by mouth once daily, only after abstaining from alcohol for at least 12 hours.
typical_duration: Used for extended periods as part of an alcohol-abstinence program under medical supervision.
directions_for_use: Never take within 12 hours of drinking alcohol.
Avoid all sources of alcohol, including cough syrups, mouthwash, sauces, and alcohol-containing topical products.
Take at the same time each day, such as in the morning.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to disulfiram or thiuram derivatives
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe disulfiram-alcohol reaction: flushing, throbbing headache, vomiting, chest pain, difficulty breathing, low blood pressure - seek emergency care immediately
Signs of liver injury: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, fatigue
Confusion, unsteady gait, or vision changes (rare neuropathy)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid all alcohol-containing products including mouthwash, cough/cold liquids, and topical rubs or perfumes applied to skin - can trigger a reaction even without drinking.
Check labels of OTC products for alcohol content before use.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for a disulfiram-alcohol reaction or signs of liver injury.
Call prescriber about persistent drowsiness or skin rash.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled liver function tests.
Avoid situations with alcohol exposure.
Consider wearing or carrying medical identification noting disulfiram use.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered that day; if not remembered until the next day, skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule - do not double up.

description: Helps maintain abstinence from alcohol in people who have already stopped drinking by reducing cravings and restoring chemical balance in the brain.
typical_dosage: Usually two 333 mg tablets three times daily, started after alcohol withdrawal and once abstinence has begun.
typical_duration: Typically continued long-term as part of an abstinence-support program, even if a relapse occurs.
directions_for_use: Take consistently, with or without food.
Continue taking even after a drinking relapse unless told otherwise by prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of suicidal thoughts or worsening depression
Severe allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Call prescriber for persistent diarrhea or mood changes.
Seek emergency care for signs of a severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track cravings and mood.
