description: A topical antibiotic ointment used to treat impetigo caused by certain bacteria.
typical_dosage: Apply a thin layer to the affected area (up to 100 cm² in adults) twice daily for 5 days.
typical_duration: Short-term use, typically 5 days.
directions_for_use: Clean the affected area gently before applying.
Apply a thin layer and may cover with a gauze dressing if directed.
Complete the full 5-day course even if the area looks improved.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of a severe allergic reaction: rash, hives, facial swelling, trouble breathing
Worsening infection, spreading redness, or fever despite treatment
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and see a prescriber if the infection worsens or signs of allergic reaction occur.
Contact the prescriber if there is no improvement within a few days.
self_monitoring: Check the treated area daily for improvement.
Complete the full prescribed 5-day course.
missed_dose_instructions: If an application is missed, simply apply at the next scheduled time; do not apply extra to make up for a missed application.

description: A topical antibacterial cream applied to burns to prevent and treat infection while the skin heals.
typical_dosage: Apply a 1/16-inch layer to clean, debrided burn areas once or twice daily, as directed.
typical_duration: Continued until the wound has adequately healed or is ready for grafting, as determined by the treating clinician.
directions_for_use: Use aseptic technique - clean hands or sterile gloves when applying.
Cleanse the wound as directed before each application; keep the area covered with the cream at all times.
Reapply promptly if cream is removed by wound drainage or bathing.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light; do not use if the cream has darkened significantly.
contraindications: Near-term pregnancy, or infants under 2 months of age (risk of kernicterus)
Known G6PD deficiency (increased risk of hemolytic anemia)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of a severe allergic reaction: rash, hives, facial swelling, trouble breathing
Signs of worsening infection: increased redness, odor, pus, fever
Blue-gray skin discoloration, unusual bruising, or signs of low blood cell counts
common_side_effects: Skin discoloration at the treated area
otc_and_other_interactions: Concurrent use with other sulfonamide medications (e.g., sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim) may increase the risk of sulfa-related side effects and should be discussed with the prescriber.
No significant OTC interactions expected beyond the above; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care for signs of a severe allergic reaction or worsening infection.
Report unusual bruising or skin/eye yellowing to the treating clinician.
self_monitoring: Monitor the wound daily for signs of healing versus infection.
Keep all follow-up wound care appointments.
missed_dose_instructions: If an application is missed, apply as soon as possible and resume the regular schedule; do not leave a burn wound uncovered for an extended period without contacting the treating clinician.

description: An antifungal cream or shampoo used to treat fungal skin infections (like ringworm or athlete's foot) or dandruff/seborrheic dermatitis of the scalp.
typical_dosage: Apply cream to the affected skin once or twice daily for 2-4 weeks, or use shampoo 2 times per week for dandruff as directed.
typical_duration: 2-4 weeks for skin infections; ongoing intermittent use for dandruff/seborrheic dermatitis as needed.
directions_for_use: Clean and dry the affected area before applying cream.
For shampoo, lather onto wet scalp/hair, leave on for about 3-5 minutes, then rinse thoroughly.
Avoid contact with the eyes; rinse with water if contact occurs.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of a severe allergic reaction: rash, hives, facial swelling, trouble breathing
Severe skin irritation, blistering, or worsening rash
common_side_effects: Itching or burning at application site
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses with topical use; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and see a prescriber/pharmacist for severe irritation or signs of allergic reaction.
See a prescriber if the infection does not improve within the expected time frame.
self_monitoring: Check the treated area or scalp for improvement.
Complete the full recommended duration of treatment for skin infections.
missed_dose_instructions: If an application is missed, simply apply/use at the next scheduled time; do not apply extra to make up for a missed application.

description: An over-the-counter antifungal cream used to treat athlete's foot, jock itch, and ringworm.
typical_dosage: Apply to the affected area twice daily for 2-4 weeks, depending on the condition being treated.
typical_duration: 2 weeks for jock itch, up to 4 weeks for athlete's foot/ringworm; see a prescriber if no improvement.
directions_for_use: Clean and dry the affected area before applying.
Apply a thin layer and gently rub in.
Continue for the full recommended duration even if symptoms improve sooner to prevent recurrence.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of a severe allergic reaction: rash, hives, facial swelling, trouble breathing
Increasing redness, swelling, or worsening of the affected area
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and see a pharmacist/prescriber for signs of allergic reaction or worsening symptoms.
See a prescriber if there is no improvement after the recommended treatment period.
self_monitoring: Check the treated area for improvement.
Keep the area clean and dry to prevent recurrence.
missed_dose_instructions: If an application is missed, simply apply at the next scheduled time; do not apply extra to make up for a missed application.

description: An over-the-counter antifungal used to treat vaginal yeast infections, or applied to the skin for athlete's foot, jock itch, and ringworm.
typical_dosage: For vaginal yeast infections, insert as a 1-, 3-, or 7-day course per product instructions; for skin infections, apply topically twice daily for 2-4 weeks.
typical_duration: 1-7 days for vaginal use depending on product strength; up to 4 weeks for skin infections.
directions_for_use: For vaginal use, insert the applicator/suppository at bedtime as directed by the product instructions.
For skin use, clean and dry the area before applying a thin layer.
Avoid tampon use during vaginal treatment; use a pad if needed for discharge.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: First-time vaginal symptoms without a prior physician-diagnosed yeast infection - see a prescriber to confirm the diagnosis
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of a severe allergic reaction: rash, hives, facial swelling, trouble breathing
Symptoms that worsen or do not improve after treatment (may indicate a different condition)
otc_and_other_interactions: Can weaken latex condoms and diaphragms - use alternative contraception protection during and for a few days after treatment.
Vaginal miconazole can increase the blood-thinning effect of warfarin, raising bleeding risk - monitor closely if used together.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and see a prescriber for signs of allergic reaction or worsening symptoms.
See a prescriber if symptoms do not resolve after completing the course, or if this is your first suspected yeast infection.
self_monitoring: Track symptom improvement over the course of treatment.
Complete the full course even if symptoms improve early.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose in a multi-day vaginal course is missed, use it as soon as remembered and continue the remaining doses; do not double up.

description: A combination cream that treats fungal skin infections (clotrimazole) while reducing associated itching and inflammation (betamethasone, a steroid).
typical_dosage: Apply a thin layer to the affected area twice daily, generally for no more than 2-4 weeks due to the steroid component.
typical_duration: Short-term use, typically limited to 2-4 weeks because of the corticosteroid component.
directions_for_use: Clean and dry the affected area before applying.
Apply a thin layer only to the affected area - avoid prolonged use beyond what is directed.
Not typically recommended for use in children due to increased steroid absorption.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to clotrimazole or betamethasone
Use under occlusive dressings without prescriber guidance
Untreated skin infections other than the one being targeted
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of skin infection worsening: increasing redness, swelling, pus, or fever
Significant skin thinning, stretch marks, or easy bruising with prolonged use
Signs of adrenal suppression with extensive/prolonged use: unusual fatigue, weight changes, weakness
common_side_effects: Thinning of the skin with prolonged use
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
Avoid combining with other topical steroid products at the same site to prevent excess steroid absorption.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and see a prescriber if the infection worsens or signs of skin thinning develop.
Do not use longer than the prescribed duration.
self_monitoring: Check the treated area regularly for improvement versus side effects.
See a prescriber if symptoms have not improved within 1-2 weeks.
missed_dose_instructions: If an application is missed, simply apply at the next scheduled time; do not apply extra to make up for a missed application.

description: An over-the-counter ointment/paste that forms a protective barrier on the skin to treat and prevent diaper rash and to protect minor skin irritation; also used as a mineral sunscreen ingredient.
typical_dosage: Apply a thick layer to the affected area with each diaper change or as needed to protect irritated skin.
typical_duration: Used as needed for skin protection; see a prescriber if a rash does not improve within 7 days.
directions_for_use: Clean and gently dry the skin before applying.
Apply liberally to fully cover the irritated area.
Do not need to fully remove old product before reapplying - clean off excess only as needed.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to zinc oxide or product ingredients
Deep or puncture wounds, or infected skin (consult a clinician first)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of skin infection: increasing redness, swelling, warmth, pus, or fever
Rash that worsens or spreads despite use
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected, as this product is not meaningfully absorbed into the bloodstream; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist if used on broken skin.
action_if_adverse_effects: Discontinue use and see a prescriber if a rash worsens, spreads, or shows signs of infection.
See a prescriber if diaper rash does not improve within 7 days.
self_monitoring: Check the skin at each application for improvement or worsening.
Keep the area clean and dry between applications.
missed_dose_instructions: This is used as needed for skin protection; there is no fixed schedule to miss.

description: A topical lotion that dries oozing skin and relieves itching from minor skin irritations such as poison ivy, insect bites, and chickenpox.
typical_dosage: Apply a thin layer to affected skin 3-4 times daily as needed.
typical_duration: Short-term use until symptoms resolve (generally no more than 7 days without consulting a pharmacist/prescriber).
directions_for_use: Shake well before use.
Apply a thin layer to clean, dry skin with a cotton ball or clean fingers.
Avoid contact with eyes, mouth, and other mucous membranes.
Do not apply to broken skin, deep wounds, or infected areas.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, tightly closed; keep away from eyes.
contraindications: Known allergy to calamine or lotion ingredients
Do not use on deep or puncture wounds, animal bites, or serious burns
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash spreading, hives, swelling, difficulty breathing
Signs of skin infection: increasing redness, warmth, pus, fever
common_side_effects: Mild stinging or burning on application
Dryness or flaking of treated skin
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
Avoid applying other topical products to the same area at the same time without pharmacist guidance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and wash off if irritation worsens or a rash develops.
Seek medical care for signs of infection or allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Watch treated area for worsening redness, swelling, or drainage.
Note whether itching improves within a few days.
missed_dose_instructions: This product is used as needed for itching; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss.

description: An antiseptic solution used to clean minor cuts, scrapes, and the skin before minor procedures to help prevent infection.
typical_dosage: Apply to the affected area 1-3 times daily, or as directed for skin preparation.
typical_duration: Short-term use for wound care until healed, generally no more than 7 days unless directed by a prescriber.
directions_for_use: Clean the area gently before applying.
Apply a small amount and allow to dry; may be covered with a bandage.
Do not use with hydrogen peroxide on the same area at the same time.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, tightly closed, away from light.
contraindications: Known iodine or shellfish-related iodine sensitivity
History of thyroid disease (use caution, especially with repeated/large-area use)
Not for use on deep puncture wounds, serious burns, or large areas of skin
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, swelling of face/lips, difficulty breathing
Signs of chemical burn or severe skin irritation
Signs of infection despite use: worsening redness, warmth, pus, fever
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid combining with hydrogen peroxide or other antiseptics on the same site - may reduce effectiveness or increase irritation.
Repeated large-area use may affect thyroid function tests; tell your prescriber if used regularly.
action_if_adverse_effects: Wash off and stop use if severe irritation, blistering, or rash occurs.
Seek care for signs of allergic reaction or worsening infection.
self_monitoring: Check the wound daily for signs of healing versus infection.
Watch for skin irritation with repeated use.
missed_dose_instructions: This product is used as needed for wound care; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss.

description: A topical antibiotic ointment used to help prevent infection in minor cuts, scrapes, and burns.
typical_dosage: Apply a small amount to the affected area 1-3 times daily.
typical_duration: Short-term use, generally no more than 7 days unless directed by a prescriber.
directions_for_use: Clean the area before applying.
Apply a thin layer and may cover with a sterile bandage.
Wash hands before and after application.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep tube tightly closed.
contraindications: Known allergy to bacitracin or other ingredients
Not for use in the eyes or for deep/serious wounds without prescriber guidance
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, itching, swelling, difficulty breathing (rare but reported with bacitracin)
Signs of worsening infection: increasing redness, swelling, pus, fever
common_side_effects: Itching or redness at application site
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
Avoid layering with other topical antibiotics on the same area.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and wash off if rash or irritation develops.
Seek care if the wound appears infected or is not improving in a few days.
self_monitoring: Check the wound for signs of healing.
Watch for new rash, itching, or spreading redness.
missed_dose_instructions: This product is used as needed for wound care; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss.

description: A combination topical antibiotic ointment used to help prevent infection in minor cuts, scrapes, and burns.
typical_dosage: Apply a small amount to the affected area 1-3 times daily.
typical_duration: Short-term use, generally no more than 7 days unless directed by a prescriber.
directions_for_use: Clean the area before applying.
Apply a thin layer; may cover with a sterile bandage.
Do not use over large areas of skin or for prolonged periods.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep tube tightly closed.
contraindications: Known allergy to neomycin, polymyxin B, bacitracin, or related antibiotics
Not for use in the eyes or ears unless a product is specifically labeled for that use
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic contact dermatitis: increasing redness, itching, rash, or swelling at the application site (common with neomycin)
Signs of a severe allergic reaction: hives, facial swelling, difficulty breathing
Signs of worsening infection: spreading redness, warmth, pus, fever
common_side_effects: Mild burning or stinging on application
Contact dermatitis (skin irritation/rash) with repeated use
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
Avoid combining with other topical antibiotics on the same area.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and wash off if a rash or worsening irritation develops; this can indicate a developing allergy.
Seek care for signs of a severe allergic reaction or a wound that appears infected.
self_monitoring: Watch for developing rash or itching, which can appear after repeated use even without prior reaction.
Check the wound for normal healing.
missed_dose_instructions: This product is used as needed for wound care; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss.

description: A topical solution/foam applied to the scalp to help regrow hair in men and women with hereditary hair thinning (androgenetic alopecia).
typical_dosage: Apply 1 mL of solution or half a capful of foam to the affected scalp area twice daily.
typical_duration: Continuous, long-term use required to maintain results; new hair growth typically takes 4 months or longer to become visible, and benefits are lost if use is stopped.
directions_for_use: Apply to a dry scalp; wash and dry hands after application.
Allow to dry completely before lying down, using other hair products, or covering the head.
Do not apply to other body areas or use more than the recommended amount.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep away from heat and open flame (solution/foam may be flammable).
contraindications: Known allergy to minoxidil or product ingredients
Scalp that is irritated, sunburned, infected, or has cuts/abrasions
Sudden or patchy hair loss of unknown cause (see a prescriber first)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Chest pain, rapid or irregular heartbeat, or lightheadedness
Unwanted facial or body hair growth
Sudden weight gain, swelling of hands/feet, or shortness of breath (possible fluid retention)
common_side_effects: Dryness or flaking of the scalp
Unwanted hair growth on adjacent skin from accidental contact
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid using other topical scalp medications (e.g., corticosteroids, retinoids) at the same time without pharmacist guidance, as this may increase absorption.
No significant systemic drug interactions expected with topical use at recommended doses.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact a prescriber for chest pain, rapid heartbeat, or swelling.
Discontinue and consult a pharmacist for persistent scalp irritation.
self_monitoring: Take a photo of the treated area periodically to track progress.
Watch for chest symptoms, irregular heartbeat, or unusual swelling.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, apply as soon as remembered; do not apply extra to make up for a missed application, and resume the normal twice-daily schedule.

description: A medicated shampoo used to control dandruff, seborrheic dermatitis, and scalp flaking.
typical_dosage: Apply to wet scalp, lather, leave on for 2-3 minutes, then rinse; use twice weekly for the first 2 weeks, then as needed to control symptoms.
typical_duration: Ongoing intermittent use as needed to control dandruff/flaking.
directions_for_use: Wet hair and scalp, apply shampoo, massage in, and let sit for the recommended time before rinsing thoroughly.
Avoid contact with eyes; rinse with water if contact occurs.
Rinse hair well after use to prevent discoloration of light or gray/dyed hair.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep tightly closed.
contraindications: Do not use on broken, inflamed, or infected scalp skin
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, facial swelling, difficulty breathing
Severe scalp irritation or burning that does not resolve
common_side_effects: Hair discoloration (temporary, especially in light/gray/treated hair)
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
Avoid using at the same time as other medicated scalp treatments unless directed.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and rinse thoroughly if irritation, rash, or eye contact occurs.
Seek care for a severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Watch for improvement in flaking/itching over 2 weeks.
Check for scalp irritation with each use.
missed_dose_instructions: This product is used intermittently as needed; there is no fixed schedule to miss - simply resume regular use.

description: A medicated shampoo used to relieve itching, flaking, and scaling from dandruff, seborrheic dermatitis, and psoriasis of the scalp.
typical_dosage: Apply to wet scalp, lather, leave on for several minutes, then rinse; use 2-3 times weekly, or as directed.
typical_duration: Ongoing intermittent use as needed to control symptoms.
directions_for_use: Wet hair, apply shampoo, massage into scalp, leave on for the time stated on the label, then rinse thoroughly.
Avoid contact with eyes.
Coal tar can increase sun sensitivity; limit sun exposure to the scalp/hairline after use.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep tightly closed.
contraindications: Acute psoriasis flare with widespread raw or oozing skin (consult prescriber first)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, facial swelling, difficulty breathing
Severe skin irritation, burning, or blistering
Signs of photosensitivity reaction (severe sunburn-like reaction after sun exposure)
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
Avoid combining with other topical scalp treatments unless directed; may increase irritation.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and rinse thoroughly if irritation or rash develops.
Seek care for signs of a severe skin reaction or sunburn-like reaction.
self_monitoring: Watch scalp for improvement in scaling/itching.
Limit sun exposure and monitor for increased sun sensitivity.
missed_dose_instructions: This product is used intermittently as needed; there is no fixed schedule to miss - simply resume regular use.

description: A topical treatment that softens and removes warts, corns, and calluses by breaking down thickened skin.
typical_dosage: Apply to the wart/callus once or twice daily, per product instructions, for up to 12 weeks.
typical_duration: Up to 12 weeks; discontinue and see a prescriber if no improvement.
directions_for_use: Soak the area in warm water for 5 minutes before application to soften skin.
Apply only to the wart/callus, avoiding surrounding healthy skin.
File away dead skin gently between applications with a pumice stone or emery board (do not share this with others).
Allow liquid/gel to dry completely before covering.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from heat; keep away from flame (may be flammable).
contraindications: Diabetes or poor circulation (do not use without prescriber guidance)
Use on moles, birthmarks, genital warts, or facial warts
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of skin infection: increasing redness, swelling, pus, warmth
Severe burning, pain, or skin breakdown beyond the treated area
Signs of salicylate toxicity with excessive/prolonged use: ringing in ears, confusion, rapid breathing (rare with proper use)
common_side_effects: Skin peeling or dryness around treated area
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
Avoid using with other topical acne or exfoliating products on the same area - may increase irritation.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and wash off if severe burning, pain, or spreading irritation occurs.
Seek care for signs of infection or if the area worsens.
self_monitoring: Check the treated area for improvement over several weeks.
Watch for irritation of surrounding healthy skin.
missed_dose_instructions: This product is used as needed per the treatment schedule; if an application is missed, resume at the next scheduled time - do not double up.

description: An eye drop used to lower elevated eye pressure in glaucoma or ocular hypertension by increasing fluid drainage from the eye.
typical_dosage: One drop in the affected eye(s) once daily in the evening.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy to control eye pressure.
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use.
Tilt head back, pull down lower eyelid, and instill one drop without touching the dropper tip to the eye or eyelid.
Press gently on the inner corner of the eye for 1 minute after instilling to reduce systemic absorption.
If using other eye drops, wait at least 5 minutes between different products.
Remove contact lenses before use and wait 15 minutes before reinserting.
storage_instructions: Store unopened bottles in the refrigerator; once opened, may be stored at room temperature for up to 6 weeks - check product labeling.
contraindications: Known allergy to latanoprost or product ingredients
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Eye pain, significant vision changes, or new light sensitivity
Signs of eye infection: redness, discharge, swelling
common_side_effects: Gradual darkening of iris color (permanent) and eyelash/eyelid skin darkening
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC eye product with a pharmacist.
Space apart from other eye drops by at least 5 minutes to avoid washing out the medication.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for persistent eye redness, pain, or vision changes.
Seek prompt care for signs of eye infection or sudden vision loss.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled eye pressure checks and eye exams.
Note any gradual changes in eye/eyelash color and report at follow-up visits.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, apply as soon as remembered that same day; do not double the next dose. If an entire day is missed, resume the normal schedule the next day.

description: An eye drop used to lower elevated eye pressure in glaucoma or ocular hypertension by reducing fluid production in the eye.
typical_dosage: One drop in the affected eye(s) once or twice daily as directed.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy to control eye pressure.
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use.
Tilt head back, pull down lower eyelid, and instill one drop without touching the dropper tip to the eye.
Press gently on the inner corner of the eye for 1-2 minutes after instilling to reduce systemic absorption.
Wait at least 5 minutes between this and other eye drops.
Remove contact lenses before use if using a preserved solution; ask a pharmacist about timing.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; protect from light.
contraindications: Severe bradycardia (slow heart rate), heart block, or uncontrolled heart failure
Known allergy to timolol or other beta blockers
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Wheezing, shortness of breath, or chest tightness
Slow or irregular heartbeat, dizziness, or fainting
Signs of low blood sugar masked in people with diabetes (this drug can blunt normal warning signs)
otc_and_other_interactions: Other oral beta blockers (e.g., metoprolol) can add to heart-rate-lowering and blood-pressure-lowering effects even when timolol is used as an eye drop.
No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for wheezing, chest tightness, or a very slow/irregular heartbeat.
Contact prescriber for persistent eye irritation or dizziness.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled eye pressure checks.
Monitor pulse if advised, especially if you also take an oral beta blocker.
People with diabetes should monitor blood sugar closely, as warning signs of low blood sugar may be reduced.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, apply as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one and resume the normal schedule - do not double up.

description: An eye drop used to lower elevated eye pressure in glaucoma or ocular hypertension by decreasing fluid production and increasing drainage.
typical_dosage: One drop in the affected eye(s) three times daily, about 8 hours apart.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy to control eye pressure.
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use.
Tilt head back and instill one drop without touching the dropper tip to the eye.
Press gently on the inner corner of the eye for 1-2 minutes after instilling.
Wait at least 5 minutes between this and other eye drops.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; protect from light.
contraindications: Infants and young children (risk of serious central nervous system depression)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Severe drowsiness, weakness, or slowed breathing (particularly important in young children if accidentally ingested/exposed)
Signs of allergic eye reaction: significant redness, swelling, itching
otc_and_other_interactions: Sedating antihistamines (e.g., diphenhydramine) may add to drowsiness.
No significant additional OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for persistent eye irritation, significant drowsiness, or dry mouth.
Seek care promptly for severe drowsiness or breathing changes, especially in a child.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled eye pressure checks.
Note excessive drowsiness or dizziness, especially when starting therapy.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, apply as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one and resume the normal schedule - do not double up.

description: An eye drop used to lower elevated eye pressure in glaucoma or ocular hypertension by reducing fluid production in the eye.
typical_dosage: One drop in the affected eye(s) three times daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy to control eye pressure.
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use.
Tilt head back and instill one drop without touching the dropper tip to the eye.
Press gently on the inner corner of the eye for 1-2 minutes after instilling.
Wait at least 5-10 minutes between this and other eye drops.
Shake well before use if directed on the label.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature (or refrigerated per label before opening); protect from light.
contraindications: Known allergy to dorzolamide or sulfonamide medications
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic/sulfa reaction: rash, hives, facial swelling, difficulty breathing
Significant eye pain, persistent blurred vision
common_side_effects: Eye stinging or burning after application
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
Space apart from other eye drops by 5-10 minutes to avoid washing out the medication.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for persistent eye irritation or vision changes.
Seek care for signs of an allergic reaction, especially if there is a known sulfa allergy.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled eye pressure checks.
Report persistent stinging, blurred vision, or unusual taste.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, apply as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one and resume the normal schedule - do not double up.

description: An eye drop used to relieve itchy, red eyes caused by allergies.
typical_dosage: One drop in the affected eye(s) once or twice daily depending on the product strength.
typical_duration: Use during allergy season or as needed; long-term use is common for chronic allergic conjunctivitis.
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use.
Tilt head back and instill one drop without touching the dropper tip to the eye.
Do not use to relieve contact lens-related irritation while lenses are in place; remove lenses before use and wait 10 minutes before reinserting (if solution contains a preservative).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep tightly closed.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of eye infection: significant redness, discharge, pain, vision changes
Signs of a severe allergic reaction
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
Space apart from other eye drops by at least 5 minutes if using multiple products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact a pharmacist or prescriber if irritation worsens or vision changes occur.
Seek care for signs of eye infection or severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track whether itching/redness improves.
Watch for eye pain or vision changes, which are not expected with normal use.
missed_dose_instructions: If used on a regular schedule and a dose is missed, apply as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; do not double up. If used as needed, there is no fixed schedule to miss.

description: An eye drop used to temporarily relieve itchy eyes caused by seasonal allergies.
typical_dosage: One drop in the affected eye(s) every 8-12 hours, up to twice daily.
typical_duration: Short-term or seasonal use; see a prescriber if symptoms persist beyond 72 hours or worsen.
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use.
Tilt head back and instill one drop without touching the dropper tip to the eye.
Remove contact lenses before use; wait at least 10 minutes before reinserting.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep tightly closed.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of eye infection: significant redness, discharge, pain, vision changes
Signs of allergic reaction: swelling, rash, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
Space apart from other eye drops by at least 5 minutes if using multiple products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use if irritation worsens and consult a pharmacist.
Seek care for eye pain, vision changes, or signs of infection.
self_monitoring: Track whether itching improves within a few days.
See a prescriber if symptoms persist beyond 72 hours.
missed_dose_instructions: This is generally used as needed for itching; if on a scheduled regimen, take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose - do not double up.

description: A lubricating eye drop used to relieve dryness, irritation, and discomfort from dry eyes.
typical_dosage: One to two drops in the affected eye(s) as needed, up to every few hours.
typical_duration: May be used as needed indefinitely for chronic dry eye, or short-term for temporary irritation.
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use.
Tilt head back and instill drops without touching the dropper tip to the eye.
If using a multi-dose bottle, do not share with others.
Contact lenses can typically remain in place with preservative-free formulas; check the product label.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; discard per label instructions after opening (often within a few weeks to months, sooner for preservative-free single-use vials).
contraindications: Known allergy to a specific product's ingredients or preservatives
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Eye pain, significant vision changes, or worsening redness (may indicate a problem other than dryness)
Signs of eye infection: discharge, swelling
common_side_effects: Temporary blurred vision immediately after use
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
Space apart from other eye medications by at least 5 minutes if using multiple products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and consult a pharmacist if stinging or irritation is persistent.
Seek care for eye pain or vision changes.
self_monitoring: Note whether dryness/irritation improves with regular use.
See a prescriber if symptoms persist despite regular use.
missed_dose_instructions: This product is used as needed; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss.

description: An antibiotic ointment applied to the eye to treat or help prevent bacterial eye infections.
typical_dosage: Apply a thin ribbon (about 1 cm) to the affected eye(s) 2-6 times daily, or as directed, for 7-10 days depending on the indication.
typical_duration: Typically 7-10 days for treatment of infection; complete the full course even if symptoms improve.
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use.
Pull down the lower eyelid and apply a thin ribbon of ointment inside the lid without touching the tube tip to the eye.
Vision may be blurred temporarily after application.
Wash hands after application to avoid spreading infection.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep tube tightly closed.
contraindications: Known allergy to erythromycin or other macrolide antibiotics
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
Worsening eye redness, pain, or vision changes despite treatment
Symptoms not improving after several days of use
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
Space apart from other eye drops/ointments by at least 10 minutes if using multiple products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber if symptoms do not improve within a few days or worsen.
Seek care for signs of an allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track improvement in redness, discharge, and irritation daily.
Complete the full prescribed course even if the eye looks better.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up. Complete the full course as prescribed.

description: An ear drop combining an antibiotic and a steroid, used to treat bacterial ear infections with inflammation, including swimmer's ear and infections with ear tubes.
typical_dosage: 4 drops in the affected ear(s) twice daily for 7 days, unless directed otherwise.
typical_duration: Typically 7 days; complete the full course even if symptoms improve.
directions_for_use: Warm the bottle in your hand before use to reduce dizziness from cold drops.
Shake well before use.
Lie down or tilt the head with the affected ear up; instill drops and keep the ear tilted up for 60 seconds; gently pull the earlobe to help drops reach the ear canal.
Avoid touching the dropper tip to the ear.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; do not freeze; keep tightly closed.
contraindications: Known allergy to ciprofloxacin, other fluoroquinolones, or corticosteroids
Viral ear infections (e.g., herpes) or fungal ear infections
Perforated eardrum, unless specifically directed by a prescriber
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, itching, swelling, difficulty breathing
Worsening ear pain, new hearing loss, or discharge despite treatment
Signs of a new fungal or other superinfection (persistent itching/discharge after completing therapy)
common_side_effects: Taste disturbance if drops reach the throat
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
Avoid using other ear drops or ear-cleaning products at the same time without pharmacist guidance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber if ear pain, drainage, or hearing changes worsen or do not improve within a few days.
Seek care for signs of an allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track improvement in ear pain and drainage daily.
Complete the full prescribed course even if symptoms improve.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: A vitamin supplement used to prevent or treat vitamin D deficiency and support bone health.
typical_dosage: 600-2,000 international units (IU) by mouth once daily for general supplementation; higher doses may be used short-term under medical supervision for documented deficiency.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing use for maintenance; higher-dose deficiency treatment is typically time-limited and directed by a prescriber.
directions_for_use: Take with a meal containing some fat to improve absorption.
Do not exceed the labeled or prescribed dose.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Known hypercalcemia (high blood calcium) or vitamin D toxicity
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of vitamin D toxicity/high calcium with excessive intake: nausea, vomiting, weakness, confusion, excessive thirst or urination, kidney problems
common_side_effects: Generally well tolerated at recommended doses
Mild GI upset in some people
otc_and_other_interactions: High-dose vitamin D can increase calcium absorption; use caution with calcium supplements or thiazide diuretics (e.g., hydrochlorothiazide), which can raise blood calcium.
May reduce effectiveness of some medications; confirm any new OTC or supplement combination with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop supplement and contact a prescriber for symptoms of high calcium (nausea, confusion, excessive thirst/urination).
Have periodic vitamin D and calcium levels checked if taking high doses long-term.
self_monitoring: Keep any scheduled vitamin D or calcium lab tests.
Avoid exceeding recommended daily intake from all combined sources (diet, sun, supplements).
missed_dose_instructions: If a daily dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule - do not double up.

description: A combination supplement providing a broad range of vitamins and minerals to help fill dietary gaps.
typical_dosage: One tablet by mouth once daily, or as directed on the product label.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing use as a dietary supplement.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce stomach upset and improve absorption of fat-soluble vitamins.
Do not exceed the labeled daily serving.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture; keep out of reach of children (iron-containing formulas can be dangerous in overdose for children).
contraindications: Conditions requiring restriction of specific vitamins/minerals (e.g., hemochromatosis and iron) - check with a prescriber first
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of vitamin/mineral overdose (rare at labeled doses): severe nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, unusual fatigue
common_side_effects: Constipation or stool color changes (with iron-containing formulas)
otc_and_other_interactions: Calcium, iron, magnesium, and zinc in multivitamins can reduce absorption of certain antibiotics (e.g., ciprofloxacin, doxycycline) if taken together - separate by at least 2 hours.
May interact with levothyroxine absorption if taken at the same time - separate doses by at least 4 hours.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact a pharmacist for persistent GI upset.
Seek care for symptoms suggesting overdose, especially in a child who may have taken multiple doses.
self_monitoring: Track overall diet and supplement use to avoid duplicating nutrients from other products.
Keep out of reach of children.
missed_dose_instructions: If a daily dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule - do not double up.

description: A combination supplement used to support bone health and help prevent or treat calcium/vitamin D deficiency and osteoporosis.
typical_dosage: 500-600 mg calcium (with vitamin D) by mouth 1-2 times daily, or as directed.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing use for bone health maintenance.
directions_for_use: Take with food to improve absorption, especially calcium carbonate formulations.
Divide doses if taking more than 500-600 mg of calcium at a time, since absorption is better in smaller doses.
Separate from iron supplements and certain antibiotics by at least 2 hours.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of high calcium: nausea, vomiting, confusion, excessive thirst/urination, muscle weakness
Signs of kidney stones: severe flank pain, blood in urine
otc_and_other_interactions: Reduces absorption of levothyroxine, ciprofloxacin, doxycycline, and other tetracycline/fluoroquinolone antibiotics if taken together - separate by at least 2-4 hours.
Thiazide diuretics (e.g., hydrochlorothiazide) can increase blood calcium when combined with calcium supplements.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for symptoms of high calcium or kidney stones.
Use a stool softener or adjust dose/timing with pharmacist guidance for constipation.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled calcium and kidney function labs if on long-term therapy.
Track bowel habits and adjust fluid/fiber intake as needed.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule - do not double up.

description: An iron supplement used to prevent or treat iron-deficiency anemia.
typical_dosage: 325 mg (65 mg elemental iron) by mouth once to three times daily, as directed.
typical_duration: Typically several months to correct deficiency; a prescriber will guide duration based on lab response.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach with water or juice (vitamin C source) for best absorption if tolerated; take with food if stomach upset occurs.
Avoid taking with dairy, calcium, antacids, or coffee/tea, which reduce absorption.
Liquid forms may stain teeth - use a straw and rinse mouth after.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture; keep tightly closed and out of reach of children (iron overdose is a leading cause of poisoning death in young children).
contraindications: Hemochromatosis or other iron overload conditions
Hemolytic anemia not due to iron deficiency
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of iron overdose (especially in children): severe vomiting, abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea, lethargy - call Poison Control or seek emergency care immediately
Severe abdominal pain or black, tarry stools that are not simply due to the iron itself (iron normally darkens stool)
common_side_effects: Dark or black stools (expected, not harmful)
otc_and_other_interactions: Antacids, calcium supplements, and dairy products reduce iron absorption - separate by at least 2 hours.
Reduces absorption of levothyroxine, ciprofloxacin, doxycycline, and other tetracycline/fluoroquinolone antibiotics - separate by at least 2-4 hours.
Vitamin C can enhance iron absorption.
action_if_adverse_effects: For constipation, increase fluids/fiber or ask a pharmacist about a stool softener.
Seek emergency care/call Poison Control for suspected overdose, especially in a child.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled hemoglobin/iron studies to track improvement.
Watch for severe GI symptoms suggesting overdose.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule - do not double up.

description: A vitamin supplement used to prevent or treat vitamin B12 deficiency, which can cause anemia and nerve problems.
typical_dosage: 500-1,000 mcg by mouth once daily for supplementation; higher doses may be used for documented deficiency under medical guidance.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing use for maintenance, especially in those with absorption problems (e.g., after certain GI surgeries, with long-term metformin or omeprazole use).
directions_for_use: May be taken with or without food.
Sublingual tablets should be allowed to dissolve under the tongue, not swallowed whole.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture and light.
contraindications: Known allergy to cobalt or vitamin B12 products
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction (rare with oral use): rash, itching, swelling, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Long-term metformin and omeprazole (or other acid reducers) use can reduce vitamin B12 absorption, increasing supplement needs.
No significant additional OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact a pharmacist for persistent GI upset.
Seek care for signs of an allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled B12 level checks if being monitored for deficiency, especially if taking metformin or long-term acid-reducing medication.
Watch for improvement in fatigue, numbness/tingling, or other deficiency symptoms.
missed_dose_instructions: If a daily dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule - do not double up.

description: A vitamin supplement used to prevent or treat folate deficiency and to reduce the risk of certain birth defects when taken before and during pregnancy.
typical_dosage: 400-800 mcg by mouth once daily for general supplementation; higher doses may be prescribed for specific medical needs.
typical_duration: Long-term for general supplementation; ongoing throughout pregnancy for prenatal use.
directions_for_use: May be taken with or without food.
Take at the same time each day for consistency.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture and light.
contraindications: Untreated vitamin B12 deficiency (folic acid can mask the anemia of B12 deficiency while nerve damage progresses) - confirm B12 status with a prescriber first if deficiency is suspected
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction (rare): rash, itching, swelling, difficulty breathing
common_side_effects: Generally well tolerated at recommended doses
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
High-dose folic acid may reduce the effectiveness of certain seizure medications; discuss with a prescriber if applicable.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact a pharmacist if a rash or unusual symptoms develop.
Seek care for signs of an allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled prenatal or deficiency-related lab work if applicable.
Report unexplained fatigue or numbness/tingling, which could indicate an underlying B12 deficiency.
missed_dose_instructions: If a daily dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule - do not double up.

description: A supplement containing omega-3 fatty acids (EPA/DHA) used to support heart health and help manage elevated triglycerides.
typical_dosage: 1,000-4,000 mg by mouth once daily, or as directed (higher doses for triglyceride management are typically supervised by a prescriber).
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing use for general supplementation or cardiovascular support.
directions_for_use: Take with meals to reduce stomach upset and fishy aftertaste.
Keep capsules refrigerated if fishy burps are bothersome (some people find this reduces the aftertaste), though this is not medically required.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature or refrigerate; protect from light and heat to prevent rancidity.
contraindications: Known fish or shellfish allergy (check product source)
Bleeding disorders or upcoming surgery, unless approved by a prescriber
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of increased bleeding: unusual bruising, blood in stool/urine, prolonged bleeding from cuts (mainly relevant at high doses or with other blood thinners)
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
common_side_effects: Mild GI upset or loose stools
otc_and_other_interactions: Can add to bleeding risk with warfarin, apixaban, clopidogrel, aspirin, or NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen), especially at higher doses.
No significant additional OTC interactions expected at typical supplement doses.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact a prescriber for signs of unusual bleeding or bruising.
Reduce dose or take with food for GI upset; consult a pharmacist if it persists.
self_monitoring: Watch for easy bruising or unusual bleeding, especially if also taking a blood thinner.
Track triglyceride levels if being used for that purpose, per prescriber follow-up.
missed_dose_instructions: If a daily dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule - do not double up.

description: A magnesium supplement used to prevent or treat magnesium deficiency and, at higher doses, to relieve occasional constipation.
typical_dosage: 250-500 mg by mouth once or twice daily for supplementation; higher doses may be used short-term for constipation as directed.
typical_duration: Long-term for supplementation; short-term (up to 1 week) if used as a laxative unless directed otherwise by a prescriber.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce stomach upset.
Drink plenty of water when using for constipation.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Severe kidney disease (risk of magnesium accumulation/toxicity)
Bowel obstruction (if used as a laxative)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of magnesium toxicity (mainly with kidney impairment or excessive use): severe weakness, very slow heartbeat, difficulty breathing, confusion
Severe or persistent diarrhea
otc_and_other_interactions: Reduces absorption of ciprofloxacin, doxycycline, and other tetracycline/fluoroquinolone antibiotics if taken together - separate by at least 2-4 hours.
May reduce absorption of levothyroxine if taken at the same time - separate by at least 4 hours.
action_if_adverse_effects: Reduce dose or stop use and contact a pharmacist for persistent diarrhea or cramping.
Seek care for signs of magnesium toxicity, especially with kidney disease.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled magnesium/kidney function labs if on long-term or high-dose therapy.
Track bowel habits if using for constipation.
missed_dose_instructions: If a daily dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule - do not double up.

description: A potassium supplement used to prevent or treat low blood potassium (hypokalemia), often caused by certain diuretics.
typical_dosage: 10-20 mEq by mouth once or twice daily, adjusted based on blood potassium levels.
typical_duration: Duration depends on the underlying cause; often long-term if taken alongside a potassium-wasting diuretic.
directions_for_use: Take with a full glass of water and with food to reduce stomach irritation.
Swallow extended-release tablets/capsules whole - do not crush, chew, or split them.
Remain upright (sitting/standing) for at least 10 minutes after taking to reduce throat irritation.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Concurrent use with potassium-sparing diuretics or salt substitutes without prescriber guidance
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of high potassium: irregular heartbeat, muscle weakness or paralysis, tingling in hands/feet/lips
Severe stomach pain, vomiting blood, or black stools (risk of GI ulceration/bleeding with extended-release potassium)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid salt substitutes and low-sodium products containing potassium chloride, which can add to the dose and cause high potassium.
ACE inhibitors, ARBs (e.g., lisinopril, losartan), and potassium-sparing diuretics (e.g., amiloride) can increase the risk of high potassium when combined.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for irregular heartbeat, severe weakness, or tingling.
Seek care immediately for severe abdominal pain or signs of GI bleeding.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled blood potassium and kidney function tests.
Report muscle weakness, palpitations, or new GI symptoms promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule - do not double up. Contact prescriber if multiple doses are missed.

description: A vitamin supplement used to prevent or treat vitamin C deficiency and support general immune and antioxidant health.
typical_dosage: 250-1,000 mg by mouth once daily, or as directed.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing use as a dietary supplement.
directions_for_use: May be taken with or without food; taking with food may reduce stomach upset at higher doses.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture and light.
contraindications: History of kidney stones (particularly oxalate stones) - use high doses with caution
Hemochromatosis or iron overload conditions (vitamin C increases iron absorption)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of kidney stones with high-dose long-term use: severe flank pain, blood in urine
common_side_effects: Stomach upset or diarrhea at high doses
otc_and_other_interactions: Increases absorption of iron supplements (may be intentional if taken together for anemia).
No significant additional OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Reduce dose and contact a pharmacist for GI upset.
Seek care for signs of kidney stones with long-term high-dose use.
self_monitoring: Avoid exceeding recommended daily intake, especially with a history of kidney stones.
Track for GI symptoms with dose changes.
missed_dose_instructions: If a daily dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule - do not double up.

description: A vitamin supplement commonly used to support healthy hair, skin, and nails, and to treat biotin deficiency.
typical_dosage: 30 mcg (RDA) to 5,000-10,000 mcg by mouth once daily, depending on the product and intended use.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing use as a dietary supplement.
directions_for_use: May be taken with or without food.
Tell your prescriber and lab staff that you take biotin before any blood tests, as high doses can interfere with certain lab test results (including some thyroid and cardiac tests).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture and light.
contraindications: No absolute contraindications at typical supplement doses; use caution with upcoming lab testing
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction (rare): rash, itching, swelling, difficulty breathing
common_side_effects: Generally well tolerated at recommended doses
otc_and_other_interactions: High-dose biotin can falsely alter results of certain lab tests, including thyroid function tests and troponin (a cardiac marker) - tell your lab and prescriber you are taking it, especially before urgent testing.
No significant additional OTC interactions expected at recommended doses.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact a pharmacist if a rash or unusual symptoms develop.
Stop biotin for the period recommended by your lab/prescriber before scheduled blood tests.
self_monitoring: Always disclose biotin use before any laboratory blood testing.
Track hair/skin/nail changes if using for that purpose (evidence for benefit without a true deficiency is limited).
missed_dose_instructions: If a daily dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule - do not double up.

description: A multivitamin formulated for use before conception and during pregnancy/breastfeeding, providing higher folic acid and iron along with other essential nutrients.
typical_dosage: One tablet/capsule by mouth once daily, or as directed by a prescriber.
typical_duration: Throughout preconception planning, pregnancy, and breastfeeding, as recommended by a prescriber.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce nausea and improve absorption.
If nausea is severe, ask your prescriber about taking at bedtime or splitting the dose.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture; keep out of reach of children (iron content can be dangerous in overdose for children).
contraindications: Iron overload conditions (discuss with prescriber if applicable)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of a significant allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
Severe constipation or abdominal pain
otc_and_other_interactions: Calcium and iron content can reduce absorption of levothyroxine and certain antibiotics (e.g., ciprofloxacin, doxycycline) if taken together - separate by at least 2-4 hours.
No other significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses.
action_if_adverse_effects: Contact prescriber for persistent nausea or constipation; do not stop without discussing alternatives.
Seek care for signs of a severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled prenatal visits and lab work.
Track nausea, constipation, and overall tolerance, and report concerns to your prescriber.
missed_dose_instructions: If a daily dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule - do not double up.

description: A combination supplement commonly used to help relieve joint pain and support joint health in osteoarthritis, though evidence for benefit is mixed.
typical_dosage: Glucosamine 1,500 mg / chondroitin 1,200 mg by mouth daily (often divided into 2-3 doses), or as directed on the product label.
typical_duration: Trial of at least 4-8 weeks to assess benefit; long-term use if helpful.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce stomach upset.
Allow several weeks of consistent use before judging effectiveness.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Known shellfish allergy (glucosamine is often derived from shellfish shells - check product source)
Use caution in people on blood thinners (see interactions)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, swelling, difficulty breathing (particularly with shellfish-derived products)
Unusual bleeding or bruising
otc_and_other_interactions: May increase the effect of warfarin, increasing bleeding risk - monitor closely if used together.
May modestly affect blood sugar; monitor if also taking metformin or glipizide.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact a prescriber for unusual bleeding or bruising, especially if taking warfarin.
Seek care for signs of an allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track joint pain/function over several weeks to judge benefit.
If on warfarin, watch for signs of increased bleeding and keep INR monitoring appointments.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule - do not double up.

description: A supplement containing beneficial live bacteria used to support digestive health and help reduce antibiotic-associated or infectious diarrhea.
typical_dosage: One capsule/packet by mouth once or twice daily, or as directed on the product label.
typical_duration: Short-term (e.g., during and after a course of antibiotics) or long-term for general digestive support, per product directions.
directions_for_use: May be taken with or without food, per product instructions.
If taking with an antibiotic, separate the doses by at least 2 hours to reduce the antibiotic killing the probiotic organisms.
storage_instructions: Store per product label - some formulations require refrigeration, others are shelf-stable; check packaging.
contraindications: Weakened immune system, central line/catheter in place, or critical illness - use only under prescriber guidance in these situations (rare but serious infection risk)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of infection in immunocompromised individuals: fever, chills (rare)
Severe or worsening abdominal pain, bloating
otc_and_other_interactions: Separate from antibiotics (e.g., amoxicillin, azithromycin, ciprofloxacin) by at least 2 hours so the antibiotic does not reduce the probiotic's effectiveness.
No other significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact a pharmacist for persistent gas, bloating, or GI upset.
Seek care for fever or signs of infection, especially if immunocompromised.
self_monitoring: Track bowel habits/GI symptoms for improvement.
Discuss use with a prescriber if immunocompromised or seriously ill.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule - do not double up.

description: A balanced electrolyte and fluid solution used to prevent or treat dehydration, especially from vomiting, diarrhea, or excessive fluid loss.
typical_dosage: Sip small amounts frequently as needed to maintain hydration; amount varies by age, weight, and degree of fluid loss - follow product label or prescriber guidance.
typical_duration: Short-term use during an episode of illness/dehydration until fluid losses resolve.
directions_for_use: Give small, frequent sips rather than large volumes at once, especially if nausea or vomiting is present.
Follow mixing instructions exactly if using powder packets - do not dilute or concentrate.
Seek medical care for infants, young children, or anyone with signs of significant dehydration (very low urine output, lethargy, sunken eyes).
storage_instructions: Store unopened product at room temperature; refrigerate opened liquid and discard per label (typically within 48 hours of opening or once frozen pops are opened).
contraindications: Kidney disease or conditions requiring fluid/electrolyte restriction - use only under prescriber guidance
Persistent vomiting preventing any fluid retention (seek medical care instead)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of ongoing significant dehydration despite use: very little/no urination, dizziness, confusion, sunken eyes, lethargy, especially in infants and young children
Signs of electrolyte imbalance: severe muscle cramps, irregular heartbeat, confusion (rare with appropriate use)
common_side_effects: Mild nausea if taken too quickly
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
Use caution combining with other electrolyte or potassium-containing supplements without guidance if kidney function is impaired.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek prompt medical care if dehydration signs persist or worsen despite use, especially in infants, young children, or older adults.
Stop and seek care for symptoms of electrolyte imbalance.
self_monitoring: Track urine output/color and overall alertness as a sign of hydration status.
Seek care promptly if vomiting/diarrhea continues beyond 24 hours or symptoms worsen.
missed_dose_instructions: This product is used as needed to maintain hydration; there is no fixed dosing schedule to miss - simply resume regular sips.

description: A medication used to treat high blood pressure and chest pain (angina) by relaxing and widening blood vessels.
typical_dosage: 20-40 mg by mouth three times daily (immediate-release), or 30-60 mg twice daily (sustained-release), titrated to response.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at evenly spaced intervals as directed, with or without food.
Swallow sustained-release capsules whole - do not crush or chew.
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture.
contraindications: Known allergy to nicardipine or other calcium channel blockers
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Chest pain that is new or worsening
Signs of very low blood pressure: severe dizziness, fainting
Significant swelling of the legs/ankles or rapid weight gain (may indicate fluid retention or worsening heart failure)
otc_and_other_interactions: Grapefruit juice can increase drug levels and side effects - avoid or limit grapefruit products.
Combined with other blood pressure medications (e.g., lisinopril, losartan, metoprolol, amlodipine) can cause additive blood-pressure-lowering and increase dizziness/fainting risk.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) can reduce the blood-pressure-lowering effect.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for chest pain, fainting, or significant swelling.
Contact prescriber for persistent headache, dizziness, or palpitations.
self_monitoring: Check blood pressure and pulse at home if recommended.
Watch for swelling of the ankles/feet and report significant changes.
Rise slowly to avoid dizziness-related falls.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: A "water pill" used, often together with other diuretics, to reduce fluid retention and help maintain normal potassium levels.
typical_dosage: 5-10 mg by mouth once daily, occasionally divided into two doses, adjusted to response.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for fluid management, unless directed otherwise.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce stomach upset.
Take earlier in the day to avoid nighttime urination.
Do not use salt substitutes containing potassium unless directed by your prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: High blood potassium (hyperkalemia) or conditions predisposing to it
Concurrent use with other potassium-sparing diuretics or potassium supplements without prescriber guidance
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of high potassium: irregular heartbeat, muscle weakness, tingling in the hands/feet/lips
Signs of dehydration or very low blood pressure: severe dizziness, fainting
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid salt substitutes/potassium supplements, which can cause dangerously high potassium when combined.
ACE inhibitors and ARBs (e.g., lisinopril, losartan) increase the risk of high potassium when combined.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) can reduce the diuretic effect and increase kidney/potassium risks.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for irregular heartbeat, severe weakness, or tingling.
Contact prescriber for persistent dizziness or fainting.
self_monitoring: Keep all scheduled potassium and kidney function labs.
Watch for muscle weakness or palpitations and report promptly.
Track daily weight if monitoring fluid status.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up. Avoid taking late in the day to prevent nighttime urination.

description: A medication used to treat high blood pressure by blocking renin, an enzyme involved in raising blood pressure.
typical_dosage: 150-300 mg by mouth once daily.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time every day, consistently either always with or always without food (high-fat meals reduce absorption).
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, protect from moisture.
contraindications: Use with ACE inhibitors or ARBs (e.g., lisinopril, losartan) in patients with diabetes or kidney impairment
History of angioedema with this medication
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Swelling of face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing/swallowing (angioedema) - seek emergency care immediately
Signs of high potassium: muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat
Signs of kidney problems: significant swelling, decreased urination
otc_and_other_interactions: Should not be combined with ACE inhibitors or ARBs (e.g., lisinopril, losartan) in people with diabetes or kidney disease due to increased risk of kidney injury, high potassium, and low blood pressure.
NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) can reduce blood-pressure-lowering effect and increase kidney risk.
Potassium supplements or salt substitutes can increase the risk of high potassium.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for facial/throat swelling or breathing trouble.
Contact prescriber for persistent diarrhea, dizziness, or signs of high potassium.
self_monitoring: Check blood pressure at home if recommended.
Keep scheduled kidney function and potassium labs.
Report unusual swelling right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.

description: A combination medication used to treat high blood pressure by slowing the heart rate and reducing fluid volume.
typical_dosage: One tablet by mouth once or twice daily, per the specific strength prescribed, titrated to blood pressure response.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time(s) each day, with or without food.
Do not stop abruptly - the beta blocker component requires gradual dose reduction to avoid rebound high blood pressure or chest pain.
Take earlier in the day if the diuretic component causes nighttime urination.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Severe bradycardia (slow heart rate), heart block, or uncontrolled heart failure
Known allergy to sulfa-derived diuretics (hydrochlorothiazide) or beta blockers
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Very slow heartbeat, dizziness, or fainting
Wheezing or difficulty breathing
Signs of low potassium or sodium: muscle cramps, severe weakness, confusion
Signs of an allergic (sulfa) reaction: rash, hives, swelling, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) can reduce the blood-pressure-lowering effect and stress the kidneys.
Other blood pressure medications (e.g., lisinopril, losartan, amlodipine) can have additive effects, increasing dizziness/fainting risk.
This medication can blunt normal warning signs (fast heartbeat) of low blood sugar in people with diabetes.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care for a very slow heartbeat, fainting, wheezing, or signs of an allergic reaction.
Contact prescriber for persistent fatigue, dizziness, or muscle cramps; do not stop abruptly.
self_monitoring: Check blood pressure and pulse at home if recommended.
Keep scheduled electrolyte and kidney function labs.
People with diabetes should monitor blood sugar closely.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up, and do not stop this medication abruptly without talking to your prescriber.

Take in the morning if the diuretic component causes nighttime urination.
