description: An antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections such as skin infections, urinary tract infections, and strep throat.
typical_dosage: 500 mg-1 g by mouth once or twice daily, depending on the infection, for 7-14 days.
typical_duration: Typically 7-14 days; complete the full course even if symptoms improve.
directions_for_use: May be taken with or without food; take with food if stomach upset occurs.
Shake oral suspension well before each use and measure with an accurate dosing device.
Complete the entire course of therapy as prescribed, even if feeling better.
storage_instructions: Store tablets/capsules at room temperature; refrigerate reconstituted oral suspension and discard after 14 days (check label).
contraindications: Known allergy to cefadroxil or other cephalosporin antibiotics
History of severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) to penicillin (use with caution due to possible cross-reactivity)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of a severe allergic reaction: hives, swelling of face/throat, difficulty breathing
Severe or bloody diarrhea, which may occur even weeks after stopping the antibiotic (possible C. difficile infection)
Signs of a severe skin reaction: blistering, peeling skin, rash with fever
otc_and_other_interactions: Can reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives in rare cases; consider a backup method during and shortly after treatment.
May enhance the effect of warfarin, increasing bleeding risk - monitor INR closely if used together.
No other significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop the medication and seek care immediately for signs of a severe allergic or skin reaction.
Contact prescriber for severe or persistent diarrhea, especially if it occurs after finishing the antibiotic.
self_monitoring: Complete the full prescribed course even if symptoms improve early.
Watch for rash, difficulty breathing, or severe diarrhea and report promptly.
If on warfarin, watch for signs of increased bleeding.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up. Complete the full course as prescribed.

description: Treats vaginal yeast infections (candidiasis) by killing the fungus causing the infection.
typical_dosage: One applicatorful of cream or one suppository inserted vaginally at bedtime for 3-7 days, depending on the product strength.
typical_duration: 3 to 7 days, as directed on the product; complete the full course even if symptoms improve.
directions_for_use: Insert the applicator or suppository high into the vagina, preferably at bedtime.
Wash hands and the applicator before and after use.
Avoid tampons, douches, and vaginal intercourse during treatment.
Continue for the full prescribed number of days even if symptoms resolve early.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; keep away from excess heat and moisture. Do not freeze.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to terconazole or other azole antifungals
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, severe itching, swelling of face/lips
Severe vaginal burning, pain, or worsening irritation
otc_and_other_interactions: The oil-based cream/suppository base may weaken latex condoms and diaphragms - use alternative contraception during treatment.
No significant systemic drug interactions expected at recommended vaginal doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact a prescriber if severe irritation, rash, or allergic symptoms occur.
Seek emergency care for facial/throat swelling or trouble breathing.
self_monitoring: Track symptom improvement; if no improvement in 3 days or symptoms worsen, contact a prescriber.
Watch for recurrent or worsening irritation.
missed_dose_instructions: Insert the missed dose as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

description: An antibiotic that stays mostly in the gut, used to treat traveler's diarrhea and IBS with diarrhea (IBS-D), and to prevent hepatic encephalopathy recurrence.
typical_dosage: 200 mg three times daily for traveler's diarrhea (3 days), or 550 mg three times daily for IBS-D (14 days, may be repeated) - as directed by prescriber.
typical_duration: Short course (3-14 days) depending on indication; some regimens may be repeated if symptoms recur.
directions_for_use: Take with or without food, at evenly spaced times.
Complete the full course even if diarrhea improves.
Do not use for diarrhea with fever or blood in the stool without medical evaluation.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to rifaximin or other rifamycin antibiotics
Fever or bloody diarrhea (may indicate a different infection requiring other treatment)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, swelling of face/throat, difficulty breathing
Diarrhea that worsens or persists despite treatment (possible C. difficile infection)
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine (mainly in patients with liver disease)
otc_and_other_interactions: Minimal systemic absorption means few significant OTC interactions; still, use anti-diarrheal products (e.g., loperamide) only as directed and confirm with a pharmacist.
Cyclosporine and other drugs that inhibit certain gut transporters can increase rifaximin absorption - report all prescription and OTC use to your pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact prescriber for worsening or bloody diarrhea, fever, or allergic symptoms.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track number and character of bowel movements.
Report new fever, blood in stool, or worsening abdominal pain promptly.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used for severe IBS with diarrhea in women who have not responded to other treatments; slows gut movement and reduces abdominal pain and diarrhea.

Stop and contact your prescriber immediately if constipation or signs of ischemic colitis (worsening abdominal pain, bloody stools) occur.

Severe constipation or inability to pass stool/gas

otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with other constipating agents (e.g., loperamide, opioid pain relievers) can increase the risk of severe constipation or bowel obstruction - avoid unless directed.
CYP1A2 inhibitors can raise alosetron levels - confirm any new OTC or herbal product with a pharmacist.

Call prescriber promptly for new or worsening constipation.
self_monitoring: Track bowel movement frequency and consistency.
Report any blood in stool or severe abdominal pain right away.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

Alcohol use disorder or heavy alcohol use

Signs of sphincter of Oddi spasm: sudden severe upper abdominal pain
Severe constipation
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid alcohol - increases risk of pancreatitis.
Combining with other opioid pain relievers (e.g., tramadol, hydrocodone) or constipating agents increases risk of severe constipation and pancreatitis-related complications.
Do not use with OTC anti-diarrheal products regularly without checking with a pharmacist.

Call prescriber for persistent constipation.
self_monitoring: Watch for new or worsening abdominal pain, especially after alcohol use.
Track bowel movement pattern.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered with food unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

description: A nasal spray that prevents allergy symptoms (sneezing, runny/itchy nose) by stopping the release of histamine from mast cells; works best when started before allergen exposure.
