description: Relieves sneezing, runny/itchy nose, itchy/watery eyes, and hives caused by seasonal or year-round allergies.
typical_dosage: 5 mg by mouth once daily (lower doses for children, per product labeling).
typical_duration: May be used seasonally for allergy symptoms or long-term for chronic hives, as directed.
directions_for_use: Take once daily, with or without food.
Orally disintegrating tablets dissolve on the tongue without water.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture and light.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to desloratadine or loratadine
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, swelling of face/throat, difficulty breathing
Severe drowsiness or fainting (uncommon)
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
Combining with other sedating antihistamines (e.g., diphenhydramine) can increase drowsiness.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care for signs of allergic reaction.
Contact prescriber if symptoms do not improve or side effects are bothersome.
self_monitoring: Track allergy symptom control.
Note any excess drowsiness, especially before driving or operating machinery.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

drug_class: Opioid analgesic (mu-opioid agonist and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor)
description: A prescription opioid pain reliever used for moderate to severe pain, including certain types of nerve pain.
typical_dosage: 50-100 mg by mouth every 4-6 hours as needed for immediate-release (max per label); extended-release dosed on a fixed schedule as directed by prescriber. Do not adjust without guidance.
typical_duration: Short-term for acute pain; longer-term use only under close prescriber supervision due to opioid risks.
directions_for_use: Take exactly as prescribed; do not crush, chew, or break extended-release tablets.
Do not increase the dose or frequency without consulting the prescriber.
Avoid alcohol while taking this medication.
storage_instructions: Store securely at room temperature, away from children and others; keep away from moisture. Dispose of unused tablets through a medication take-back program.
contraindications: Significant respiratory depression or severe asthma without monitoring
Known or suspected gastrointestinal obstruction (including paralytic ileus)
Use of MAOIs (e.g., phenelzine, selegiline) within the past 14 days
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Slow, shallow, or stopped breathing; extreme drowsiness or unresponsiveness - seek emergency care immediately
Signs of serotonin syndrome: agitation, rapid heartbeat, fever, muscle rigidity, sweating
Signs of severe allergic reaction: swelling of face/throat, difficulty breathing
Symptoms of physical dependence, misuse, or overdose
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid alcohol and other sedating OTC products (e.g., diphenhydramine-containing sleep aids) - increased risk of dangerous sedation and slowed breathing.
Combining with other opioids, benzodiazepines, or muscle relaxants increases risk of severe sedation and respiratory depression.
Never combine with MAOIs (phenelzine, selegiline) - risk of serotonin syndrome or dangerous blood pressure changes.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for slowed/stopped breathing or unresponsiveness (naloxone may be needed).
Call prescriber for signs of serotonin syndrome or bothersome side effects.
Do not stop abruptly after prolonged use without medical guidance due to withdrawal risk.
self_monitoring: Track pain control and level of alertness.
Watch for signs of constipation and consider a stool softener if advised.
Keep opioid medication secured and count remaining tablets.
missed_dose_instructions: For as-needed use, there is no fixed schedule to miss - take only when needed for pain per prescriber instructions. For scheduled dosing, take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; do not double up.

description: A skin patch that delivers an antidepressant medication (MAOI class) used to treat major depressive disorder.
typical_dosage: One patch applied to dry, intact skin once every 24 hours; dose individualized by prescriber. Do not adjust without guidance.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed; do not stop abruptly.
directions_for_use: Apply to a clean, dry area of skin on the upper torso, upper thigh, or outer upper arm; rotate application sites.
Apply at the same time each day and remove after 24 hours before applying a new patch.
At the lowest (6 mg) dose, strict dietary tyramine restriction is generally not required, but follow prescriber's specific dietary guidance at higher doses.
Avoid exposing the patch application site to direct heat sources (heating pads, sunbathing).
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in the original pouch; dispose of used patches by folding sticky sides together and keeping away from children and pets (patches retain drug after use).
contraindications: Use with other MAOIs, SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclic antidepressants, tramadol/tapentadol, or St. John's Wort - risk of serotonin syndrome or hypertensive crisis
Use with meperidine, dextromethorphan, or certain other drugs affecting serotonin
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of hypertensive crisis: severe headache, chest pain, stiff neck, nausea/vomiting, rapid heartbeat - seek emergency care immediately
Signs of serotonin syndrome: agitation, confusion, rapid heartbeat, fever, muscle rigidity
New or worsening depression, suicidal thoughts, or unusual behavior changes
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid decongestants and cough/cold products containing pseudoephedrine, phenylephrine, or dextromethorphan - risk of dangerous blood pressure spikes or serotonin syndrome.
Avoid St. John's Wort and other serotonergic supplements.
At higher doses, tyramine-rich foods (aged cheese, cured meats, tap beer) can cause a hypertensive crisis - follow prescriber's dietary guidance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for signs of hypertensive crisis or serotonin syndrome.
Contact prescriber for new or worsening mood changes or severe application site reactions.
Do not stop or start any new medication or supplement without checking with prescriber/pharmacist.
self_monitoring: Monitor blood pressure if recommended.
Watch for mood changes, especially early in treatment or after dose changes.
Check application site daily for irritation.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply a new patch as soon as remembered and resume the regular daily schedule; contact the prescriber if unsure rather than doubling up or applying two patches.

description: An oral antidepressant used for depression that has not responded to other treatments; works by blocking the breakdown of certain brain chemicals.
typical_dosage: 15 mg by mouth 2-3 times daily, titrated by prescriber up to a maximum as tolerated. Do not adjust without guidance.
typical_duration: Long-term therapy as directed; do not stop abruptly.
directions_for_use: Take consistently as prescribed, with or without food.
Follow a strict low-tyramine diet as instructed by prescriber/pharmacist for the duration of treatment and for 2 weeks after stopping.
Avoid alcohol, especially tap beer and red wine.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture and light.
contraindications: Use with other MAOIs, SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclic antidepressants, tramadol/tapentadol, or St. John's Wort - risk of serotonin syndrome
Use with sympathomimetics (including many decongestants) - risk of hypertensive crisis
Pheochromocytoma, severe heart failure, or liver disease
Use within 14 days of stopping (or starting) another MAOI or serotonergic drug
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of hypertensive crisis: severe headache, chest pain, stiff neck, vomiting, rapid or irregular heartbeat - seek emergency care immediately
Signs of serotonin syndrome: agitation, confusion, rapid heartbeat, fever, muscle rigidity, tremor
New or worsening depression, suicidal thoughts, or unusual behavior changes
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid all decongestants (pseudoephedrine, phenylephrine), many cough/cold and diet products, and stimulants - risk of hypertensive crisis.
Avoid tyramine-rich foods (aged cheeses, cured/fermented meats, tap beer, soy sauce, sauerkraut) - risk of hypertensive crisis.
Avoid St. John's Wort and other serotonergic herbal supplements - risk of serotonin syndrome.
Confirm every new OTC medication, herbal product, or supplement with a pharmacist before use.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for signs of hypertensive crisis or serotonin syndrome.
Contact prescriber for worsening mood, suicidal thoughts, or signs of liver problems.
Do not stop abruptly; discuss any discontinuation plan with prescriber.
self_monitoring: Monitor blood pressure regularly if recommended.
Watch closely for mood changes, especially when starting or changing dose.
Keep a list of all foods, OTC products, and medications avoided while on this drug.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

description: Used alone or with other medications to control partial-onset (focal) seizures in adults and children.
typical_dosage: Starting dose and titration individualized by prescriber, typically reaching 100-200 mg twice daily; do not adjust without guidance.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for seizure control as directed.
directions_for_use: Take at the same times each day, with or without food.
Do not stop abruptly - this can trigger increased seizure frequency or status epilepticus; taper only under prescriber guidance.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Known second- or third-degree AV heart block (unless paced)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of irregular heartbeat, fainting, or severe dizziness (possible PR interval prolongation)
New or worsening suicidal thoughts or behavior changes
Signs of severe allergic/multi-organ reaction: rash, fever, swollen glands, facial swelling (DRESS syndrome)
Increased seizure frequency
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with alcohol or other sedating OTC products (e.g., diphenhydramine-containing sleep aids) increases dizziness and drowsiness.
Use with other drugs that affect heart rhythm/PR interval should be discussed with a prescriber.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for fainting, irregular heartbeat, or signs of severe allergic/skin reaction.
Contact prescriber promptly for mood changes or increased seizures.
Do not stop the medication suddenly.
self_monitoring: Keep a seizure log noting frequency and severity.
Report dizziness that affects safe driving or daily activities.
Watch for mood or behavior changes.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up. Contact prescriber if multiple doses are missed.

drug_class: Non-stimulant ADHD medication (selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor)
description: A non-stimulant medication used to treat attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children, adolescents, and adults.
typical_dosage: Dosing individualized by age and titrated by prescriber, typically starting at 100-200 mg once daily; do not adjust without guidance.
typical_duration: Ongoing therapy as directed; effectiveness and dose reassessed periodically by prescriber.
directions_for_use: Take once daily, with or without food, at about the same time each day.
Swallow capsules whole, or open and sprinkle on food as directed if unable to swallow whole.
Do not stop abruptly without prescriber guidance.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Use with MAOIs or within 14 days of stopping an MAOI
severe_side_effects_seek_care: New or worsening suicidal thoughts or behavior, especially in children/adolescents - seek care immediately
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue
Fast or irregular heartbeat, significant blood pressure changes
Sleepiness severe enough to impair activities such as driving
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid combining with MAOIs.
Sedating OTC products (e.g., diphenhydramine-containing sleep aids) may increase drowsiness.
Confirm any new OTC or herbal supplement with a pharmacist, as this drug affects certain liver enzyme pathways.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek care immediately for suicidal thoughts, severe drowsiness, or signs of liver problems.
Contact prescriber for bothersome side effects before stopping on your own.
self_monitoring: Track ADHD symptom control and daily functioning.
Monitor mood, especially in children/adolescents, and report changes promptly.
Watch for excessive sleepiness affecting school, work, or driving safety.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

description: Taken regularly to help prevent migraine headaches by blocking a protein (CGRP) involved in migraine attacks.
typical_dosage: 10-60 mg by mouth once daily, as determined by prescriber.
typical_duration: Long-term preventive use as directed; benefit assessed after several weeks to months.
directions_for_use: Take once daily at about the same time, with or without food.
This is a preventive medication, not for treating a migraine attack already in progress.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: rash, swelling of face/throat, difficulty breathing
Signs of liver problems (uncommon): yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe fatigue
otc_and_other_interactions: St. John's Wort and other strong CYP3A4 inducers can significantly reduce atogepant's effectiveness - avoid combining without prescriber guidance.
No other significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Contact prescriber for persistent constipation, nausea, or signs of liver problems.
self_monitoring: Keep a headache/migraine diary to track frequency and severity.
Report new or worsening constipation or fatigue.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

drug_class: Prostaglandin E1 analog (erectile dysfunction agent, non-oral)
description: Used to treat erectile dysfunction by relaxing blood vessels and increasing blood flow to the penis; given as a self-injection or a small urethral pellet, not as a pill.
typical_dosage: Dose individualized and titrated by the prescriber, starting with a low test dose in the office; do not adjust the dose without guidance.
typical_duration: Used as needed, generally no more than once daily and limited times per week as directed by prescriber.
directions_for_use: Use exactly as taught by the prescriber for injection technique or urethral application.
Do not use more often than directed - overuse increases risk of prolonged erection (priapism) and scarring.
Rotate injection sites/urethral technique as instructed.
storage_instructions: Store as directed on the product labeling; some formulations require refrigeration - check the specific product insert.
contraindications: Conditions predisposing to priapism (e.g., sickle cell disease/trait, multiple myeloma, leukemia)
Men for whom sexual activity is inadvisable
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Erection lasting longer than 4 hours (priapism) - seek emergency care immediately
Severe or worsening pain at the injection/application site
Signs of fibrosis or curvature of the penis with continued use
common_side_effects: Pain at the injection or application site
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with oral erectile dysfunction medications (e.g., sildenafil) or other vasodilators can increase the risk of low blood pressure and prolonged erection - avoid unless specifically directed by prescriber.
No significant routine OTC interactions expected otherwise; confirm any new OTC product with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for an erection lasting more than 4 hours.
Contact prescriber for severe site pain or penile curvature/lumps.
self_monitoring: Note duration of erections and seek care if prolonged.
Inspect injection/application sites for excessive bruising or lumps.
missed_dose_instructions: This is used as needed before sexual activity, not on a fixed schedule - there is no missed dose to make up.

description: Relaxes the bladder muscle to reduce urinary urgency, frequency, and leakage associated with overactive bladder.
typical_dosage: 1-2 mg twice daily (immediate-release) or 2-4 mg once daily (extended-release), as directed.
typical_duration: Ongoing use as directed; effectiveness reassessed periodically.
directions_for_use: Take with water; extended-release capsules should be swallowed whole.
Take at the same time(s) each day.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Inability to urinate or severe lower abdominal pain
Severe eye pain, vision changes, or halos around lights (possible angle-closure glaucoma)
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling of face/throat, difficulty breathing
Confusion or severe drowsiness, particularly in older adults
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with other anticholinergic OTC products (e.g., diphenhydramine-containing sleep aids/allergy products) increases risk of confusion, severe dry mouth, constipation, and urinary retention - especially in older adults.
Avoid or use caution with other drugs that have anticholinergic effects.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for inability to urinate, severe eye pain, or allergic reaction.
Contact prescriber for bothersome dry mouth, constipation, or confusion.
self_monitoring: Track urinary symptoms and any difficulty urinating.
Watch for confusion or excessive drowsiness, especially in older adults.
Maintain adequate fluid and fiber intake to offset constipation.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

description: Relaxes the bladder muscle to reduce urinary urgency, frequency, and leakage associated with overactive bladder.
typical_dosage: 20 mg twice daily on an empty stomach (immediate-release) or 60 mg once daily in the morning (extended-release).
typical_duration: Ongoing use as directed; effectiveness reassessed periodically.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before meals.
Swallow extended-release capsules whole; do not crush or chew.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Inability to urinate or severe lower abdominal pain
Severe eye pain, vision changes, or halos around lights
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling of face/throat, difficulty breathing
Confusion or severe drowsiness, particularly in older adults
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with other anticholinergic OTC products (e.g., diphenhydramine-containing sleep aids/allergy products) increases risk of confusion, severe dry mouth, constipation, and urinary retention - especially in older adults.
Take apart from meals; food can reduce absorption of this medication.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for inability to urinate, severe eye pain, or allergic reaction.
Contact prescriber for bothersome dry mouth, constipation, or confusion.
self_monitoring: Track urinary symptoms and any difficulty urinating.
Watch for confusion or excessive drowsiness, especially in older adults.
Maintain adequate fluid and fiber intake to offset constipation.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose or meal timing has passed; then skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

description: Relaxes the bladder muscle to reduce urinary urgency, frequency, and leakage associated with overactive bladder.
typical_dosage: 7.5-15 mg by mouth once daily.
typical_duration: Ongoing use as directed; effectiveness reassessed periodically.
directions_for_use: Take once daily, with or without food.
Swallow tablets whole; do not crush or chew.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Inability to urinate or severe lower abdominal pain
Severe eye pain, vision changes, or halos around lights
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling of face/throat, difficulty breathing
Confusion or severe drowsiness, particularly in older adults
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with other anticholinergic OTC products (e.g., diphenhydramine-containing sleep aids/allergy products) increases risk of confusion, severe dry mouth, constipation, and urinary retention - especially in older adults.
Grapefruit juice and certain other substances that affect drug-metabolizing enzymes may raise levels - confirm with a pharmacist if you regularly consume grapefruit products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for inability to urinate, severe eye pain, or allergic reaction.
Contact prescriber for bothersome dry mouth, constipation, or confusion.
self_monitoring: Track urinary symptoms and any difficulty urinating.
Watch for confusion or excessive drowsiness, especially in older adults.
Maintain adequate fluid and fiber intake to offset constipation.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

description: Relaxes muscles in the prostate and bladder neck to improve urine flow in men with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH).
typical_dosage: 8 mg by mouth once daily with a meal (4 mg daily in moderate kidney impairment).
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy for BPH symptoms as directed.
directions_for_use: Take with the same meal each day to reduce stomach upset.
Swallow capsule whole; do not crush, chew, or open.
Rise slowly from sitting or lying down to reduce dizziness.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Concurrent use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors in patients with kidney impairment
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fainting or severe dizziness, especially when standing up
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling of face/throat, difficulty breathing
Painful or prolonged erection (priapism, rare)
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with erectile dysfunction medications (e.g., sildenafil) can cause a significant drop in blood pressure - use lowest effective doses and space administration as advised.
Other blood pressure medications (e.g., amlodipine, lisinopril, losartan) may add to blood-pressure-lowering and dizziness effects.
Tell your surgeon you take this drug before any cataract/eye surgery (intraoperative floppy iris syndrome risk).
action_if_adverse_effects: Sit or lie down immediately if feeling faint or dizzy; seek care if fainting occurs.
Seek emergency care for signs of allergic reaction or a prolonged erection.
self_monitoring: Track urinary symptom improvement.
Watch for dizziness, especially with position changes or after starting other new medications.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and resume the regular schedule with the next meal; do not double up.

description: A combination medication that shrinks the prostate over time and relaxes prostate/bladder muscle to improve urinary symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH).
typical_dosage: One capsule by mouth once daily, about 30 minutes after the same meal each day.
typical_duration: Long-term therapy; full benefit on prostate size may take up to 6 months.
directions_for_use: Take about 30 minutes after the same meal each day.
Swallow capsule whole; do not crush, chew, or open - contents can irritate the mouth/throat.
Women who are pregnant or may become pregnant should not handle leaking or broken capsules.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture and out of reach of women who are or may become pregnant.
contraindications: Women and children (not indicated for use)
Known hypersensitivity to dutasteride, tamsulosin, or other alpha blockers/5-alpha-reductase inhibitors
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Fainting or severe dizziness, especially when standing
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling of face/throat, difficulty breathing
Painful or prolonged erection (priapism, rare)
Breast lumps, pain, or nipple discharge (rare, report to prescriber)
otc_and_other_interactions: Combining with erectile dysfunction medications (e.g., sildenafil) can cause a significant drop in blood pressure.
Other blood pressure medications (e.g., amlodipine, lisinopril, losartan) may add to blood-pressure-lowering and dizziness effects.
Tell your surgeon you take this drug before any cataract/eye surgery (intraoperative floppy iris syndrome risk).
This medication can lower PSA (prostate blood test) results - tell your prescriber you take it before any PSA testing.
action_if_adverse_effects: Sit or lie down immediately if feeling faint or dizzy; seek care if fainting occurs.
Seek emergency care for signs of allergic reaction or a prolonged erection.
Report any breast changes to your prescriber.
self_monitoring: Track urinary symptom improvement over months.
Watch for dizziness, especially with position changes.
Report sexual side effects to prescriber if bothersome.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, skip it and resume the regular schedule with the next meal; do not double up.

description: A topical medication that reduces inflammation and bacteria to treat acne and the redness/bumps of rosacea.
typical_dosage: Apply a thin layer to affected skin twice daily (morning and evening), or as directed.
typical_duration: Improvement typically seen after several weeks; continued use as directed for maintenance.
directions_for_use: Wash and dry the affected area gently before application.
Apply a thin layer and gently massage in; wash hands after use.
Avoid contact with eyes, mouth, and mucous membranes; rinse with water if contact occurs.
Use sunscreen during the day, as skin may be more sensitive to sun.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; do not freeze.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to azelaic acid or product components
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: widespread rash, swelling, difficulty breathing (rare)
Severe skin irritation, blistering, or worsening redness that doesn't improve
common_side_effects: Redness or itching at application site
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid using at the same time as other irritating topical acne products (e.g., benzoyl peroxide, strong retinoids) without spacing applications, as this can increase skin irritation.
No significant systemic drug interactions expected with topical use; confirm any new topical OTC product with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact prescriber for severe irritation, blistering, or allergic symptoms.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track skin appearance and tolerance over several weeks.
Watch for excessive dryness or irritation and adjust frequency with prescriber guidance if needed.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply the missed dose as soon as remembered unless close to the next application; then skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double apply.

description: A topical cream used to treat the inflammatory bumps and lesions of rosacea by reducing skin mites and inflammation.
typical_dosage: Apply a pea-sized amount to the affected areas of the face once daily.
typical_duration: Improvement typically seen after 1-3 months of continued use.
directions_for_use: Apply a thin layer once daily to the affected facial areas, avoiding the eyes, lips, and mucous membranes.
Wash hands after application.
Wait for the cream to dry before applying makeup or sunscreen.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; do not freeze.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to ivermectin or product components
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: widespread rash, swelling of face, difficulty breathing (rare)
Severe skin burning, irritation, or worsening of rosacea symptoms
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant systemic drug interactions expected with topical use; confirm any new topical OTC product with a pharmacist.
Avoid combining with other irritating topical products on the same area without prescriber guidance.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact prescriber for severe irritation or worsening symptoms.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track rosacea symptom improvement over 1-3 months.
Watch for skin irritation and report if bothersome.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply the missed dose as soon as remembered; if close to the next scheduled application, skip the missed one and resume the regular schedule. Do not double apply.

description: A topical antibiotic gel/cream that reduces the redness and bumps of rosacea.
typical_dosage: Apply a thin layer to affected areas once or twice daily, as directed.
typical_duration: Improvement typically seen after 3-9 weeks; continued use as directed for maintenance.
directions_for_use: Wash and dry the affected area gently before application.
Apply a thin layer and avoid the eyes and mucous membranes.
Use sunscreen, as rosacea-prone skin may be sun-sensitive.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; do not freeze.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to metronidazole or product components
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: widespread rash, swelling, difficulty breathing (rare)
Severe skin irritation, burning, or worsening redness
otc_and_other_interactions: Although absorption through the skin is minimal, avoid alcohol during treatment and for at least 1 day after stopping - can cause flushing, nausea, and rapid heartbeat similar to the reaction seen with oral metronidazole.
No other significant systemic interactions expected with topical use; confirm any new topical OTC product with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact prescriber for severe irritation or allergic symptoms.
Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
self_monitoring: Track rosacea symptom improvement over several weeks.
Watch for skin irritation and report if bothersome.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply the missed dose as soon as remembered; if close to the next scheduled application, skip the missed one and resume the regular schedule. Do not double apply.

description: A topical gel that temporarily reduces the facial redness of rosacea by narrowing blood vessels in the skin.
typical_dosage: Apply a pea-sized amount to each of five areas of the face (forehead, chin, nose, each cheek) once daily.
typical_duration: Effect on redness is temporary (up to 12 hours per application); used daily for ongoing redness control.
directions_for_use: Apply a thin, even layer once daily; wait for it to dry before applying other products or makeup.
Wash hands immediately after application.
Avoid contact with eyes, lips, and mucous membranes.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature; do not freeze.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to brimonidine or product components
Use with MAOIs (e.g., phenelzine, selegiline) - risk of significant blood pressure changes
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Worsening redness, flushing, or a burning sensation that spreads beyond the application area (rebound erythema)
Signs of significant blood pressure or heart rate changes: fainting, chest pain, irregular heartbeat
Signs of severe allergic reaction: swelling, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid use with MAOIs (phenelzine, selegiline) - can cause significant blood pressure changes.
Other blood-pressure-affecting medications (e.g., amlodipine, lisinopril, losartan, metoprolol) may have additive effects; use caution and inform your pharmacist.
No significant OTC interactions expected otherwise at recommended topical doses.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact prescriber for worsening redness, burning, or allergic symptoms.
Seek emergency care for fainting, chest pain, or irregular heartbeat.
self_monitoring: Track facial redness control throughout the day.
Watch for rebound redness that worsens as the effect wears off.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply the missed dose as soon as remembered; if close to the next scheduled application, skip the missed one and resume the regular schedule. Do not double apply.

description: An injectable biologic medication that reduces inflammation to treat plaque psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, and certain other inflammatory conditions.
typical_dosage: Dosing individualized by condition, typically 150-300 mg subcutaneously at weeks 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, then monthly; do not adjust without guidance.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by prescriber.
directions_for_use: Bring the syringe/pen to room temperature (about 15-30 minutes) before injecting; do not warm any other way.
Inject into the thigh, abdomen (avoiding 2 inches around the navel), or upper arm, rotating sites.
Do not shake the device; inspect for particles or discoloration before use.
storage_instructions: Store in the refrigerator; do not freeze. May be stored at room temperature for a limited time per product labeling - protect from light and do not return to the refrigerator once warmed.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of serious infection: fever, chills, persistent cough, wounds that won't heal
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, swelling of face/throat, difficulty breathing - seek emergency care immediately
New or worsening inflammatory bowel disease symptoms (abdominal pain, diarrhea, blood in stool)
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid live vaccines while on this medication - discuss vaccination timing with your prescriber.

No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC or herbal product with a pharmacist, since immune-stimulating supplements (e.g., echinacea) could theoretically counteract the intended immune-modulating effect.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Contact prescriber promptly for signs of infection or new bowel symptoms.
self_monitoring: Watch for any signs of infection and report them promptly.
Track psoriasis/arthritis symptom improvement.
Inspect injection sites for excessive redness or swelling.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, contact the prescriber's office for guidance on when to give the next dose rather than guessing or doubling up.

description: An injectable biologic medication that reduces inflammation to treat moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis.
typical_dosage: 100 mg subcutaneously at week 0, week 4, then every 8 weeks, as determined by prescriber.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy as directed by prescriber.
directions_for_use: Bring the syringe/pen to room temperature (about 30 minutes) before injecting; do not warm any other way.
Inject into the thigh or abdomen (avoiding 2 inches around the navel), rotating injection sites.
Do not shake the device; inspect for particles or discoloration before use.
storage_instructions: Store in the refrigerator; do not freeze. May be stored at room temperature for a limited time per product labeling.
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of serious infection: fever, chills, persistent cough, wounds that won't heal
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, swelling of face/throat, difficulty breathing - seek emergency care immediately
otc_and_other_interactions: Avoid live vaccines while on this medication - discuss vaccination timing with your prescriber.

No significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC or herbal product with a pharmacist, since immune-stimulating supplements (e.g., echinacea) could theoretically counteract the intended immune-modulating effect.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of severe allergic reaction.
Contact prescriber promptly for signs of infection.
self_monitoring: Watch for any signs of infection and report them promptly.
Track psoriasis/arthritis symptom improvement.
Inspect injection sites for excessive redness or swelling.
missed_dose_instructions: If a dose is missed, contact the prescriber's office for guidance on when to give the next dose rather than guessing or doubling up.

description: Eye drops that reduce inflammation to increase the eye's own tear production in chronic dry eye disease.
typical_dosage: One drop in each eye twice daily, about 12 hours apart.
typical_duration: Long-term use; full effect on tear production may take up to 6 months.
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use; do not let the vial tip touch the eye or any surface.
If wearing contact lenses, remove before applying and wait at least 15 minutes before reinserting.
Use one vial per application to each eye and discard the remainder - do not reuse opened vials.
If using other eye drops, wait at least 15 minutes between products.
storage_instructions: Store unopened vials at room temperature in the original foil pouch; discard opened vials after use.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to cyclosporine or product components
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of eye infection: increasing redness, pain, discharge, or vision changes
Severe or worsening eye pain
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant systemic drug interactions expected with ophthalmic use; confirm any new OTC eye product (including artificial tears) with a pharmacist and space administration by at least 15 minutes.
Avoid using other eye medications at the same time without spacing them apart.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact prescriber for signs of eye infection or worsening pain.
Contact prescriber if burning/stinging is severe or persistent.
self_monitoring: Track dry eye symptom improvement over months.
Watch for signs of eye infection or new vision changes.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply the missed dose as soon as remembered unless close to the next scheduled dose; then skip and resume the regular twice-daily schedule. Do not double up.

drug_class: Ophthalmic immunomodulator (LFA-1 antagonist, dry eye agent)
description: Eye drops that reduce inflammation associated with dry eye disease, helping relieve eye dryness, burning, and irritation.
typical_dosage: One drop in each eye twice daily, about 12 hours apart.
typical_duration: Ongoing use as directed; symptom improvement may be noticed within weeks.
directions_for_use: Wash hands before use; do not let the vial tip touch the eye or any surface.
Remove contact lenses before use and wait at least 15 minutes before reinserting.
Use one vial per application to each eye and discard the remainder.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature in the original foil pouch until ready to use; discard opened vials after use.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to lifitegrast or product components
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of eye infection: increasing redness, pain, discharge, or vision changes
Signs of allergic reaction: swelling, severe eye irritation
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant systemic drug interactions expected with ophthalmic use; confirm any new OTC eye product (including artificial tears) with a pharmacist and space administration by at least 15 minutes.
Avoid using other eye medications at the same time without spacing them apart.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact prescriber for signs of eye infection or allergic reaction.
Contact prescriber if eye irritation is severe or persistent.
self_monitoring: Track dry eye symptom improvement.
Watch for signs of eye infection or new vision changes.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply the missed dose as soon as remembered unless close to the next scheduled dose; then skip and resume the regular twice-daily schedule. Do not double up.

description: An over-the-counter ear drop that releases oxygen to soften and break up earwax for easier removal.
typical_dosage: 5-10 drops into the affected ear twice daily for up to 4 days, as directed on the label.
typical_duration: Up to 4 consecutive days; if earwax buildup persists, see a healthcare provider.
directions_for_use: Tilt the head sideways or lie down with the affected ear facing up.
Place the drops into the ear canal; keep the ear tilted up for a few minutes, or place a cotton ball in the ear.
Do not insert the applicator tip directly into the ear canal.
Flush the ear with warm water afterward if directed by the product label.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture; keep the bottle tightly closed.
contraindications: Ear pain, drainage/discharge, or suspected perforated eardrum
Ear tubes or recent ear surgery
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Ear pain, drainage, or worsening hearing loss during or after use
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling, severe itching
common_side_effects: Mild ear discomfort or a bubbling/fizzing sensation
Temporary mild itching in the ear canal
otc_and_other_interactions: No significant systemic drug interactions expected with otic use; confirm any new OTC ear product with a pharmacist.
Do not use at the same time as other ear drops unless directed by a healthcare provider.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and contact a healthcare provider if ear pain, drainage, or hearing changes occur.
Seek care if symptoms do not improve after 4 days of use.
self_monitoring: Watch for ear pain, discharge, or hearing changes during treatment.
If wax buildup persists after treatment, see a healthcare provider for removal.
missed_dose_instructions: This is used on an as-needed short-term basis; if a scheduled dose is missed, apply as soon as remembered and continue the regular twice-daily schedule for the remaining days.

description: A vaginal gel form of the hormone progesterone, used to support the uterine lining in fertility treatment and for certain menstrual/hormone conditions.
typical_dosage: One applicatorful (typically 4% or 8% gel) inserted vaginally once daily, or as directed by prescriber based on treatment protocol.
typical_duration: Duration depends on the specific fertility or hormonal treatment protocol, as directed by prescriber.
directions_for_use: Insert using the prefilled applicator as instructed; a small amount of residue may remain in the vagina after use, which is expected.
Use at the same time each day.
Avoid use with certain vaginal products at the same time unless directed - check with your pharmacist.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture and heat.
contraindications: Known or suspected breast cancer or other hormone-sensitive cancer
Active or history of blood clots (deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, stroke)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clot: leg swelling/pain, chest pain, shortness of breath, sudden severe headache, vision changes, or weakness on one side - seek emergency care immediately
Severe abdominal pain or unusual vaginal bleeding
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, swelling, difficulty breathing
otc_and_other_interactions: St. John's Wort can reduce hormone levels/effectiveness via liver enzyme induction - avoid combining without discussing with prescriber.
No other significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC or herbal product with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for signs of blood clot.
Contact prescriber for unusual bleeding, severe abdominal pain, or bothersome side effects.
self_monitoring: Track any unusual bleeding, leg swelling, or severe headaches.
Follow up with prescriber per fertility/hormone treatment monitoring schedule.
missed_dose_instructions: Insert the missed dose as soon as remembered; if close to the next scheduled dose, contact your prescriber's office for guidance rather than doubling up, since timing may be important to your treatment protocol.

description: An oral progestin hormone used to treat abnormal uterine bleeding, endometriosis, and to delay menstruation.
typical_dosage: Dosing individualized by indication, commonly 2.5-15 mg by mouth daily as directed by prescriber.
typical_duration: Duration depends on indication (cyclic or continuous), as directed by prescriber.
directions_for_use: Take at the same time each day, with or without food.
Follow the specific schedule (cyclic vs. continuous) given by your prescriber.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Known or suspected breast cancer or other hormone-sensitive cancer
Active or history of blood clots (DVT, pulmonary embolism, stroke)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clot: leg swelling/pain, chest pain, shortness of breath, sudden severe headache, vision changes, or one-sided weakness - seek emergency care immediately
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine, severe abdominal pain
Unusual or heavy vaginal bleeding
otc_and_other_interactions: St. John's Wort can reduce the effectiveness of this medication via liver enzyme induction, potentially leading to breakthrough bleeding or reduced hormonal control - avoid combining without discussing with prescriber.
No other significant OTC interactions expected at recommended doses; confirm any new OTC or herbal product with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for signs of blood clot.
Contact prescriber for unusual bleeding, signs of liver problems, or bothersome side effects.
self_monitoring: Track menstrual bleeding pattern and report unusual changes.
Watch for leg swelling, chest pain, or severe headaches.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up. Missed doses can cause breakthrough bleeding.

description: An injectable hormone therapy that lowers estrogen or testosterone levels, used to treat endometriosis, uterine fibroids, and prostate cancer, among other conditions.
dosage_forms: Injection (depot/extended-release, administered by a healthcare provider)
typical_dosage: Dosing is individualized and administered/titrated by the prescriber on a monthly, 3-month, 4-month, or 6-month depot schedule depending on the product and indication; do not adjust the dose or schedule without guidance.
typical_duration: Duration depends on the condition being treated, as directed by prescriber; may range from several months to longer-term therapy.
directions_for_use: This medication is given by a healthcare provider in a clinic or office setting - it is not self-administered at home in most formulations.
Keep all scheduled injection appointments to maintain hormone suppression.
Report symptoms of a temporary 'flare' (worsening symptoms) that can occur in the first few weeks of treatment.
storage_instructions: Storage is handled by the administering clinic/pharmacy per product-specific requirements (some formulations require refrigeration).
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of a heart rhythm problem: fainting, chest pain, irregular or rapid heartbeat (this drug class can prolong the QT interval)
Severe bone pain or new fractures (bone density loss with long-term use)
Signs of depression or significant mood changes
Severe hot flashes with dizziness or fainting
common_side_effects: Decreased bone density with long-term use
otc_and_other_interactions: Other medications that can affect heart rhythm (e.g., ondansetron) may add to the risk of QT interval prolongation - tell your prescriber and pharmacist about all medications you take.
No significant routine OTC interactions expected otherwise; confirm any new OTC or herbal product with a pharmacist.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for fainting, chest pain, or irregular heartbeat.
Contact prescriber for severe bone pain, mood changes, or bothersome hot flashes.
self_monitoring: Keep all follow-up appointments and bone density testing as scheduled.
Track mood changes and hot flash severity.
Report any irregular heartbeat or fainting episodes.
missed_dose_instructions: This is a scheduled injectable given by a healthcare provider - if an appointment is missed, contact the prescriber's office promptly to reschedule rather than guessing when to resume.

description: A topical testosterone solution used to treat low testosterone (hypogonadism) in men.
typical_dosage: Dosing individualized and titrated by prescriber based on blood testosterone levels, typically applied once daily to the underarms; do not adjust without guidance.
typical_duration: Long-term, ongoing therapy with periodic monitoring as directed.
directions_for_use: Apply to clean, dry, intact underarm skin using the provided applicator; do not apply to other body areas.
Wash hands immediately after application.
Allow the application site to dry completely before dressing; cover the area with clothing once dry.

Avoid swimming or showering for at least 2 hours after application, and avoid skin-to-skin contact with others (especially women and children) at the application site to prevent unintentional transfer.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from heat and open flame (contains alcohol and is flammable).
contraindications: Known or suspected prostate or breast cancer
Pregnant or breastfeeding women should avoid contact with application sites
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of blood clot: leg swelling/pain, chest pain, shortness of breath - seek emergency care immediately
Prolonged or painful erection
Signs of stroke or heart attack: chest pain, difficulty speaking, weakness on one side, shortness of breath
Significant mood changes, aggression, or new/worsening sleep apnea
Signs of unintended exposure in a child or partner (e.g., early puberty signs, unusual hair growth) - seek medical evaluation
otc_and_other_interactions: Can increase the blood-thinning effect of warfarin - increased bleeding risk; more frequent INR monitoring may be needed.
Confirm any new OTC or herbal product with a pharmacist, as some supplements marketed for 'testosterone support' may have unpredictable additive effects.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care for signs of blood clot, stroke, or heart attack, or a prolonged erection.
Contact prescriber for significant mood changes or signs of transfer to another person.
self_monitoring: Keep scheduled blood tests for testosterone levels, blood counts, and prostate monitoring.
Watch for swelling, chest pain, or shortness of breath.
Ensure the application site is fully dry and covered to prevent transfer to others.
missed_dose_instructions: Apply the missed dose as soon as remembered that day; if not remembered until the next day, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not apply extra to make up for a missed dose.

description: An essential fat-soluble vitamin and antioxidant used as a dietary supplement to address or prevent vitamin E deficiency; also commonly taken for general health, though high-dose benefits beyond treating deficiency are not well established.
typical_dosage: Typical supplement doses range from 100-400 IU daily; do not exceed labeled amounts without discussing with a healthcare provider, as high doses (generally above 400 IU/day) may increase bleeding risk.
typical_duration: Ongoing as a daily supplement, or as directed for a diagnosed deficiency.
directions_for_use: Take with a meal containing some fat to improve absorption, since it is fat-soluble.
Do not exceed the recommended dose on the label unless directed by a healthcare provider.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from heat, light, and moisture.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to vitamin E supplements
Use caution with high doses in people with bleeding disorders or those on blood thinners
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of unusual bleeding or bruising, especially at high doses or when combined with blood thinners
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, difficulty breathing (rare)
otc_and_other_interactions: High doses can increase the blood-thinning effect of warfarin, apixaban, clopidogrel, and aspirin/NSAIDs, raising bleeding risk - discuss any vitamin E use above standard daily amounts with a pharmacist if taking these medications.

As with all dietary supplements, vitamin E products are not regulated by the FDA with the same rigor as prescription drugs, so potency and purity can vary between brands - choose reputable, third-party-tested products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care for unusual bleeding, bruising, or allergic symptoms.
Contact a pharmacist or prescriber before combining with blood thinners.
self_monitoring: Watch for unusual bruising or bleeding, especially if also taking blood thinners.
Report any new symptoms to a healthcare provider.
missed_dose_instructions: This is generally taken as a daily supplement; if a dose is missed, take it when remembered unless it is close to the next dose, then skip it - do not double up.

description: A calcium supplement used to prevent or treat low calcium intake and to support bone health, often recommended alongside vitamin D.
typical_dosage: Typically 500-1200 mg of elemental calcium daily in divided doses, per label directions or as recommended by a healthcare provider.
typical_duration: Ongoing as a daily supplement, as directed.
directions_for_use: Calcium citrate can be taken with or without food (unlike calcium carbonate, which needs food for absorption).
Divide larger total daily doses into 2-3 smaller doses for better absorption.
Separate from other medications known to interact (see interactions) by at least 2-4 hours.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture.
contraindications: Severe kidney disease or kidney stones (calcium-containing) without provider guidance
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of high calcium: confusion, severe nausea/vomiting, muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat
Signs of kidney stones: severe flank or back pain, blood in urine
otc_and_other_interactions: Reduces absorption of levothyroxine, ciprofloxacin, and certain other antibiotics/thyroid medications - separate doses by at least 4 hours (levothyroxine) or 2-6 hours (ciprofloxacin) as directed by a pharmacist.
Can reduce absorption of iron supplements if taken together - separate doses if both are needed.
As with all dietary supplements, this product is not regulated by the FDA with the same rigor as prescription drugs, so potency can vary between brands.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care for signs of high calcium or kidney stones.
Contact a pharmacist about timing if you take thyroid medication or certain antibiotics.
self_monitoring: Track total daily calcium intake from food and supplements to avoid exceeding recommended limits.
Report new or worsening constipation.
missed_dose_instructions: This is generally taken as a daily supplement; if a dose is missed, take it when remembered unless it is close to the next dose, then skip it - do not double up.

description: An iron supplement used to treat or prevent iron deficiency anemia.
typical_dosage: Dosing individualized based on the degree of iron deficiency, typically 50-150 mg of elemental iron daily, as directed by label or prescriber.
typical_duration: Often several months to correct deficiency and replenish iron stores; duration confirmed by follow-up bloodwork.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach for best absorption if tolerated; take with food if it causes stomach upset.
Avoid taking with dairy products, calcium supplements, or antacids, which can reduce absorption.
Vitamin C (e.g., orange juice) can enhance iron absorption if taken together.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture; keep tightly closed and away from children (iron overdose is dangerous in children).
contraindications: Hemochromatosis or other iron overload conditions
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of iron overdose (especially in children): severe stomach pain, vomiting (possibly bloody), diarrhea - seek emergency care immediately
Severe constipation or black, tarry stools with abdominal pain that seems unusual for you
common_side_effects: Dark or black-colored stools (expected, not harmful)
otc_and_other_interactions: Reduces absorption of levothyroxine and certain antibiotics such as ciprofloxacin - separate dosing by at least 4 hours (levothyroxine) or 2-6 hours (ciprofloxacin).
Calcium supplements and acid-reducing medications (e.g., omeprazole, vonoprazan) can reduce iron absorption - space doses apart as advised by a pharmacist.

As with all dietary supplements, iron products are not regulated by the FDA with the same rigor as prescription drugs, so potency can vary between brands - keep out of reach of children due to overdose risk.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for signs of iron overdose, especially in a child.
Contact prescriber for severe constipation or unusual abdominal pain.
self_monitoring: Follow up on blood counts/iron studies as recommended.
Track bowel habits and manage constipation with fluids/fiber as needed.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

description: An iron supplement used to treat or prevent iron deficiency anemia.
typical_dosage: Dosing individualized based on the degree of iron deficiency, typically providing 30-60 mg of elemental iron once or twice daily, as directed by label or prescriber.
typical_duration: Often several months to correct deficiency and replenish iron stores; duration confirmed by follow-up bloodwork.
directions_for_use: Take on an empty stomach for best absorption if tolerated; take with food if it causes stomach upset.
Avoid taking with dairy products, calcium supplements, or antacids, which can reduce absorption.
Vitamin C (e.g., orange juice) can enhance iron absorption if taken together.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture; keep tightly closed and away from children (iron overdose is dangerous in children).
contraindications: Hemochromatosis or other iron overload conditions
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of iron overdose (especially in children): severe stomach pain, vomiting (possibly bloody), diarrhea - seek emergency care immediately
Severe constipation or black, tarry stools with abdominal pain that seems unusual for you
common_side_effects: Dark or black-colored stools (expected, not harmful)
otc_and_other_interactions: Reduces absorption of levothyroxine and certain antibiotics such as ciprofloxacin - separate dosing by at least 4 hours (levothyroxine) or 2-6 hours (ciprofloxacin).
Calcium supplements and acid-reducing medications (e.g., omeprazole, vonoprazan) can reduce iron absorption - space doses apart as advised by a pharmacist.

As with all dietary supplements, iron products are not regulated by the FDA with the same rigor as prescription drugs, so potency can vary between brands - keep out of reach of children due to overdose risk.
action_if_adverse_effects: Seek emergency care immediately for signs of iron overdose, especially in a child.
Contact prescriber for severe constipation or unusual abdominal pain.
self_monitoring: Follow up on blood counts/iron studies as recommended.
Track bowel habits and manage constipation with fluids/fiber as needed.
missed_dose_instructions: Take as soon as remembered unless close to the next dose; then skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.

description: An herbal supplement traditionally used to help with occasional sleeplessness and mild anxiety; evidence for effectiveness is limited compared to conventional medications.
typical_dosage: Typically 300-600 mg of extract taken 30-60 minutes before bedtime, or as directed on the product label.
typical_duration: Generally intended for short-term, occasional use for sleep; discuss with a healthcare provider if used regularly for more than a few weeks.
directions_for_use: Take about 30-60 minutes before bedtime.
Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you, as it can cause daytime drowsiness.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture and light.
contraindications: Use caution in those with liver disease (rare reports of liver effects)
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of severe allergic reaction: rash, hives, swelling, difficulty breathing (rare)
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine (rare)
Excessive daytime drowsiness affecting safety
otc_and_other_interactions: Increases sedation risk when combined with other CNS depressants, including alcohol, sleep aids (e.g., diphenhydramine), benzodiazepines (e.g., alprazolam), and opioid pain relievers (e.g., tramadol, hydrocodone/acetaminophen) - avoid combining without guidance.

As with all herbal supplements, valerian is not regulated by the FDA with the same rigor as prescription drugs, so potency and purity can vary between brands; discontinue gradually rather than abruptly after prolonged use.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care for signs of allergic reaction or liver problems.
Avoid driving or hazardous activities if drowsy.
self_monitoring: Track sleep quality and daytime alertness.
Note any interaction with other sedating medications or alcohol.
missed_dose_instructions: This is generally used as needed before bedtime, so there is no fixed dose to miss; simply take it on nights it is needed.

description: An herbal supplement derived from the turmeric spice, commonly used for its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, including for joint discomfort.
typical_dosage: Typically 500-2000 mg of turmeric extract (standardized for curcumin content) daily in divided doses, or as directed on the product label.
typical_duration: Often used for weeks to months; discuss long-term use with a healthcare provider.
directions_for_use: Take with food, ideally containing some fat, to improve absorption.
Products combined with black pepper extract (piperine) may increase absorption.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture and light.
contraindications: Gallbladder disease or bile duct obstruction (can stimulate bile production)
Use caution before scheduled surgery due to bleeding risk
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of unusual bleeding or bruising
Signs of liver problems: yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine (rare, especially with high-dose products)
Severe abdominal pain (possible gallstone-related symptoms)
otc_and_other_interactions: Has mild antiplatelet activity and can increase bleeding risk when combined with warfarin, apixaban, clopidogrel, aspirin, or NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) - use caution and discuss with a pharmacist, especially before surgery or dental procedures.
As with all herbal supplements, turmeric/curcumin products are not regulated by the FDA with the same rigor as prescription drugs, so potency and purity can vary between brands.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care for unusual bleeding, bruising, or signs of liver problems.
Contact prescriber before surgery if taking regularly.
self_monitoring: Watch for unusual bruising or bleeding, especially if also taking blood thinners or NSAIDs.
Report new abdominal pain, especially in the upper right area.
missed_dose_instructions: This is generally taken as a daily supplement; if a dose is missed, take it when remembered unless it is close to the next dose, then skip it - do not double up.

description: An herbal supplement derived from elderberry fruit, commonly used to help reduce the duration/severity of cold and flu symptoms by supporting immune response.
typical_dosage: Follow product label directions, commonly 1 tablespoon of syrup (or equivalent gummies/capsules) 1-4 times daily during illness, or as directed.
typical_duration: Typically used short-term at the onset of cold/flu symptoms, for up to about 5 days, unless otherwise directed.
directions_for_use: Take at the first sign of cold or flu symptoms for best effect.
Ensure raw, uncooked, or unripe elderberry (not the processed commercial product) is never consumed, as it can be toxic - only use properly prepared commercial products.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature or as directed on the label; refrigerate liquid products after opening if instructed.
contraindications: Autoimmune conditions (may theoretically stimulate immune activity) - discuss with prescriber before use
Use caution in patients on immunosuppressant therapy
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, swelling, difficulty breathing (rare)
Signs of unusually low blood sugar if also taking diabetes medications: shakiness, sweating, confusion
otc_and_other_interactions: May lower blood sugar - can have additive effects with diabetes medications such as glipizide, increasing the risk of hypoglycemia; monitor blood sugar closely if used together.

May stimulate immune activity, which could theoretically reduce the effectiveness of immunosuppressant medications such as prednisone or biologic therapies - discuss with prescriber if on such treatment.

As with all herbal supplements, elderberry products are not regulated by the FDA with the same rigor as prescription drugs, so potency and purity can vary between brands - use only properly processed commercial products.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care for signs of allergic reaction.
Monitor blood sugar closely and contact prescriber if on diabetes medication and experiencing low blood sugar symptoms.
self_monitoring: Track cold/flu symptom duration and severity.
Monitor blood sugar if diabetic and using this supplement.
missed_dose_instructions: This is generally used as needed at the onset of cold/flu symptoms, so there is no fixed dose to miss; simply resume the regular schedule at the next planned dose.

description: An herbal supplement commonly used at the onset of a cold to potentially shorten its duration or reduce symptom severity, though evidence of benefit is mixed.
typical_dosage: Follow product label directions, as formulations and concentrations vary widely between products.
typical_duration: Typically used short-term (up to about 10-14 days) at the onset of cold symptoms; not generally recommended for continuous long-term use.
directions_for_use: Start at the first sign of cold symptoms for potential benefit.
Avoid continuous long-term daily use; take breaks between courses of use as advised on the label.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture and light.
contraindications: Known allergy to plants in the daisy (Asteraceae) family, such as ragweed, marigolds, or chrysanthemums
Autoimmune conditions (may theoretically stimulate immune activity) - discuss with prescriber before use
Use caution in patients on immunosuppressant therapy
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, swelling of face/throat, difficulty breathing - especially in those with ragweed/daisy family allergies
Signs of liver problems (rare): yellowing skin/eyes, dark urine
otc_and_other_interactions: May stimulate immune activity, which could theoretically reduce the effectiveness of immunosuppressant medications such as prednisone or biologic therapies - discuss with prescriber if on such treatment.

As with all herbal supplements, echinacea products are not regulated by the FDA with the same rigor as prescription drugs, so potency and purity can vary significantly between brands and species used.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek care immediately for signs of allergic reaction.
Contact prescriber if on immunosuppressant therapy and considering use.
self_monitoring: Track cold symptom duration and severity.
Watch for allergic symptoms, especially if you have known plant/pollen allergies.
missed_dose_instructions: This is generally used as needed at the onset of cold symptoms, so there is no fixed dose to miss; simply resume the regular schedule at the next planned dose.

description: An herbal supplement sometimes used for mild low mood; it has numerous significant interactions with prescription medications and should not be started without discussing it with a pharmacist or prescriber.
typical_dosage: Follow product label directions, commonly 300 mg standardized extract taken 2-3 times daily; formulations and potency vary widely between products.
typical_duration: Effects on mood, if any, may take several weeks to become apparent; discuss appropriate duration with a healthcare provider.
directions_for_use: Take with food to reduce stomach upset.
Do not start this supplement without checking with a pharmacist or prescriber first, due to numerous significant drug interactions.
Use sun protection, as this supplement can increase sensitivity to sunlight.
storage_instructions: Store at room temperature, away from moisture and light.
contraindications: Use with MAOIs, SSRIs, SNRIs, tramadol/tapentadol, or other serotonergic drugs - risk of serotonin syndrome
Use with hormonal contraceptives, certain HIV medications, transplant anti-rejection drugs, or many other drugs metabolized by the liver - can cause treatment failure
Planned surgery (can interact with anesthesia-related medications) - discuss stopping before surgery with your care team
Known hypersensitivity to St. John's Wort
severe_side_effects_seek_care: Signs of serotonin syndrome: agitation, rapid heartbeat, fever, muscle rigidity, sweating - especially if combined with antidepressants or tramadol
Signs of allergic reaction: rash, hives, swelling, difficulty breathing
Severe sun sensitivity/burning
otc_and_other_interactions: Major interaction: reduces the effectiveness of many prescription drugs (including warfarin, apixaban, sildenafil, alprazolam, statins such as simvastatin/atorvastatin, and hormonal contraceptives/progestins) by inducing liver enzymes that break these drugs down faster - this can lead to treatment failure or, for anticoagulants, breakthrough clotting.
Combined with SSRIs (sertraline, escitalopram), tramadol, or other serotonergic drugs, increases the risk of serotonin syndrome - avoid combining without medical guidance.

As with all herbal supplements, St. John's Wort products are not regulated by the FDA with the same rigor as prescription drugs, so potency and purity can vary significantly between brands, making interaction risk harder to predict.
Always tell your pharmacist and every prescriber that you take St. John's Wort before starting or stopping it, since it interacts with a very wide range of medications.
action_if_adverse_effects: Stop use and seek emergency care for signs of serotonin syndrome or severe allergic reaction.
Contact prescriber before stopping or starting this supplement if you take other prescription medications, since sudden changes can affect drug levels.
self_monitoring: Watch for reduced effectiveness of any prescription medication you take (e.g., breakthrough bleeding on hormonal therapy, reduced anticoagulation).
Track mood changes and report worsening depression or suicidal thoughts to a prescriber.
Watch for signs of serotonin syndrome if taking any antidepressant or tramadol/tapentadol.
missed_dose_instructions: This is generally taken as a daily supplement; if a dose is missed, take it when remembered unless it is close to the next dose, then skip it - do not double up.
